chunks.text:
This guide shows you how to run SightPress on your own computer, create your first website and sign in to its admin
panel, so that you can try it out. You don't need to know how to program. It takes about 30 minutes, most of which is
waiting for downloads.

!!! note "What you can try today"

    You can create a website with ready-made pages, write, schedule and publish pages, translate them into other
    languages, upload pictures and other files, invite people or let them sign up, make pages members-only, search
    the website, read its visitor statistics, turn features on or off, change its theme, colours and page layouts, add
    captions and transcripts, keep files in the cloud, and set up an optional AI assistant with your own key. Running SightPress on a public server is not covered yet.

chunks.heading: What you need
chunks.text:
- A computer running Windows 10 or 11, macOS, or Linux.
- About 5 GB of free disk space.
- An internet connection.
- Permission to install programs on the computer.

You type some commands in a terminal. A terminal is a window where you type instructions instead of clicking:

- On Windows, open **Windows Terminal** or **PowerShell** from the Start menu.
- On macOS, open **Terminal** from Applications, then Utilities.
- On Linux, open your terminal app.

Type or paste each command, then press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.

chunks.heading: Step 1: install Docker
chunks.text:
Docker runs SightPress and everything it needs inside separate, self-contained boxes called containers. You don't
have to install PHP, a web server or a database yourself.

1. Install Docker:
    - On Windows or macOS, install [Docker Desktop](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/). On Windows, accept the
      option to use WSL 2 if the installer asks.
    - On Linux, install [Docker Engine and the Docker Compose plugin](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/).
2. On Windows or macOS, open Docker Desktop and wait until it says that Docker is running.
3. In the terminal, type:

    ```sh
    docker compose version
    ```

    You should see a line such as `Docker Compose version v5.3.0`. The number may be different. If you see
    "command not found" or a similar message, Docker is not installed correctly, or Docker Desktop is not running.

chunks.heading: Step 2: install Git
chunks.text:
Git downloads the SightPress files from GitHub, where they are published.

1. Install Git from the [Git downloads page](https://git-scm.com/downloads). On macOS, you can instead type
   `git --version` in the terminal and accept the offer to install the developer tools.
2. In the terminal, type:

    ```sh
    git --version
    ```

    You should see a line such as `git version 2.51.0`.

chunks.heading: Step 3: download SightPress
chunks.text:
You only download the `skeleton`, the project you start. The other parts of SightPress are fetched for you
automatically the first time you start it, in step 4.

1. Make a folder for SightPress and go into it:

    ```sh
    mkdir sightpress
    cd sightpress
    ```

2. Download the skeleton:

    ```sh
    git clone https://github.com/sightpress/skeleton.git
    ```

    You should see a few lines that end with `done.`

3. Go into the `skeleton` folder:

    ```sh
    cd skeleton
    ```

!!! tip "Only on Linux"

    The SightPress container writes files as user number 1000. If your Linux user has a different number, files
    can end up owned by the wrong user. Type `id -u`. If it shows anything other than `1000`, copy the settings
    file with `cp .env.example .env`, open `.env` in a text editor, and set `UID` and `GID` to the numbers that
    `id -u` and `id -g` show. Windows and macOS users can skip this.

chunks.heading: Step 4: start SightPress
chunks.text:
1. In the `skeleton` folder, type:

    ```sh
    docker compose up
    ```

2. Wait. The first time, Docker downloads and builds everything it needs. This can take 5 to 15 minutes. You see
   many lines of text scroll past. Later starts take a few seconds.
3. SightPress is ready when the text stops scrolling and you see lines starting with `php-1` that end with
   `ready to handle connections`.

Leave this terminal window open. SightPress stops when you close it.

chunks.heading: Step 5: open SightPress in your browser
chunks.text:
1. Open your web browser and go to <http://localhost:8080>.
2. You should see a plain page with the heading **No site configured** and this text: "SightPress is running, but
   no site is set up for this address yet. If you look after this server, create a site and link this address to
   it." The browser tab is called "No site configured - SightPress".

This is the right result. It means SightPress is running, but has no website yet. You create one in the next steps.

If the browser shows **502 Bad Gateway**, SightPress is still finishing its first start. Wait a minute, then
reload the page.

chunks.heading: Step 6: make a settings file with a secret key
chunks.text:
SightPress keeps its settings in a file called `.env` in the `skeleton` folder. One setting, the secret key, protects
the address of each website's database. You make it once.

1. Open a second terminal window and go to the `skeleton` folder, as in step 3. Leave the first window running.
2. Copy the example settings file:

    ```sh
    cp .env.example .env
    ```

3. Make a secret key:

    ```sh
    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php php -r 'echo bin2hex(random_bytes(32)), PHP_EOL;'
    ```

    You should see one line of 64 letters and digits, such as `3f9a…`. Yours will be different.

4. Open the `.env` file in a text editor, such as Notepad on Windows or TextEdit on macOS. Find the line
   `APP_SECRET=` and paste your key straight after the `=` sign, with no spaces. Save the file.
5. Keep a copy of the key somewhere safe, such as a password manager. Without it, SightPress can't open your
   websites' databases.
6. Go back to the first terminal window and press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> to stop SightPress. Then start it
   again with `docker compose up`, so that it reads the new settings.

The copied file also turns on the test e-mail inbox, which catches every e-mail SightPress sends. See
[Open the test e-mail inbox](how-to/open-the-test-email-inbox.md).

chunks.heading: Step 7: create your first website
chunks.text:
1. In the second terminal window, type this command on one line. Change the e-mail address and the names to your
   own if you like. (You can also type just `docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:create` and
   answer one question at a time: see [Create a website](how-to/create-a-site.md).)

    ```sh
    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:create demo --domain=localhost --db=sqlite:////app/sites/demo.sqlite --url=http://localhost:8080 --owner-type=organization --locale=en-GB --name="Riverside Library" --admin-email=ada@example.org --admin-first-name=Ada --admin-last-name=Lovelace
    ```

2. After a few seconds, you should see lines like these:

    ```text

    Gave the first admin the admin role.

    Made the site's icons, wordmark and share image from its name; replace them with site:branding:set.
    Published the starter pages in British English: Welcome to Riverside Library, About us, Contact us, Privacy notice, Terms of use, Accessibility statement.
    Added 5 starter pages to the main and footer menus.
    The

chunks.heading: Step 8: choose your password and sign in
chunks.text:
1. In your browser, go to <http://localhost:8080/login/setup>. You should see the heading **Set up your account**.
2. In **Email address**, type the address you used, for example `ada@example.org`.
3. In **6-digit code**, type the setup code. You can type it with or without the space.
4. Choose **Continue**. You should see the heading **Choose your password**.
5. In **New password**, type a password of at least 12 characters. A few unrelated words make a strong password
   that is easy to remember.
6. Choose **Set password**. You should see the sign-in page with the message "Your password has been set. Sign in
   with it now."
7. Type your e-mail address and your new password, then choose **Sign in**.
8. You should see the admin panel's **Dashboard**. The browser tab says "Dashboard - Admin - Riverside Library".
   The admin menu has links such as Dashboard, Pages, Analytics, Redirects, Media, Menus, People, Invite someone,
   Site settings, Features and Audit log.

SightPress never sends links to sign in or to set a password. It always gives you a code to type on the website
instead. See [Codes we send you](how-to/codes-we-send-you.md).

chunks.heading: Step 9: look at your website
chunks.text:
1. Go to <http://localhost:8080>.
2. You should see the home page, with the heading **Welcome to Riverside Library**, a main menu with About us and
   Contact us, and a footer menu with the privacy notice, the terms of use and the accessibility statement.

Every new website starts with these six pages, already published. Change them in the admin panel under **Pages**.
See [Write and publish a page](how-to/write-and-publish-a-page.md).

The pages follow your computer's light or dark setting, and every page works with a keyboard alone and with a
screen reader. While SightPress runs on your computer, every page asks search engines not to list it.

chunks.heading: Step 10: stop SightPress
chunks.text:
1. Go back to the terminal window where SightPress is running.
2. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>. You should see lines that end with `Stopped`.

To start SightPress again later, go to the `skeleton` folder and type `docker compose up` again. Your website and
your account are kept.

chunks.heading: If something goes wrong
chunks.text:
**"port is already allocated" or "address already in use"**
:   Another program on your computer is using one of the ports SightPress needs. See
    [Change the ports SightPress uses](how-to/change-the-ports.md).

**"Cannot connect to the Docker daemon"**
:   Docker is not running. On Windows or macOS, open Docker Desktop and wait until it says that Docker is running.
    On Linux, type `sudo systemctl start docker`.

**The page doesn't load at all**
:   Check that the terminal still shows SightPress running, and that the address is exactly
    `http://localhost:8080`, with `http`, not `https`.

**"APP_SECRET is not set" when you create the site**
:   The secret key is missing from `.env`. Go back to [step 6](#step-6-make-a-settings-file-with-a-secret-key).

**The website shows an error page after you created it**
:   SightPress was not restarted after you added the secret key. Stop it with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> and
    start it again with `docker compose up`.

**"This code doesn't work" on the setup page**
:   Check the e-mail address and the six digits. A setup code works once, for 7 days. To get a new one, see
    [Create a website](how-to/create-a-site.md#give-someone-a-new-setup-code).

chunks.heading: What to do next
chunks.text:
The [how-to guides](how-to/index.md) show you how to write and publish pages, add a language and translate a page,
schedule, move or restore pages, make a site members-only, let people sign up, turn features on or off, search the
website, read its analytics, set up the AI assistant and run SightPress in the background. To move an older
installation to this version, see [Update SightPress](how-to/update-sightpress.md).

To start your website in more than one language, give `site:create` a list in `--locale`, for example
`--locale=en-GB,pt-PT`: every starter page is then written in each language. See
[Add a language and translate a page](how-to/add-a-language.md) to add one later, and
[Turn features on or off](how-to/turn-features-on-or-off.md) to choose the optional features.

You can help improve SightPress without being a developer: see [Report a problem](how-to/report-a-problem.md) and
the other guides under *Help improve SightPress*.

To change how your website looks, see [Install and change a theme](how-to/install-and-change-a-theme.md) and
[Choose a page layout](how-to/choose-a-page-layout.md). Your files are kept in the `sites` folder on your computer. To
keep them elsewhere, see [Keep your files in the cloud](how-to/keep-files-in-the-cloud.md). For big files, see
[Upload large files](how-to/upload-large-files.md) and [Import files from a folder](how-to/import-files.md). To make
videos and recordings accessible, see [Add captions and transcripts](how-to/add-captions-and

chunks.heading: Who can do what
chunks.text:
You are the website's first **Admin**: you can do everything. When you invite people, give each one the lowest role
that lets them do their work: **Editor** to check and publish pages, **Contributor** to write pages that need approval,
or **Member** to read members-only pages. If none fits, make your own under **Roles** in the admin menu: see
[Create a custom role](how-to/create-a-custom-role.md).

chunks.heading: Add features
chunks.text:
Under **Features**, turn the built-in features on or off for this website. To add a feature that SightPress doesn't
have, install a module: see [Add a module](how-to/add-a-module.md). To keep every website and account to your
organisation's email addresses, see [Keep websites to your organisation](how-to/keep-websites-to-your-organisation.md).

chunks.heading: Sign in with your phone
chunks.text:
Text messages are off on your computer, so you sign in with your email address. Once whoever runs SightPress
[sets up text messages](how-to/set-up-text-messages.md), you can
[add your mobile number](how-to/add-your-mobile-number.md),
[sign in with your phone](how-to/sign-in-with-your-phone.md), get
[notifications by text](how-to/text-message-notifications.md) and
[confirm important changes](how-to/confirm-important-changes.md) with a code. If you lose your phone, see
[Lost your phone](how-to/lost-your-phone.md).

The reference pages explain [roles](reference/roles-and-permissions.md), [blocks](reference/blocks.md),
[search and AI visibility](reference/search-and-ai.md) and the [command line tool](reference/command-line.md).

chunks.page: Add a language and translate a page
chunks.text:
A website can be written in several languages. Each page then has one **translation** per language, with its own
title, address and content. Visitors read the page in their language, and search engines are told which pages are
translations of each other.

You need to be an **admin** to add a language, and an **editor** or **admin** to publish a translation. Contributors
can write translations; an editor publishes them.

chunks.page: Add a language and translate a page
chunks.heading: Add a language
chunks.text:
1. Sign in to the admin panel, for example at <http://localhost:8080/admin>.
2. Choose **Site settings** in the admin menu, then **Change the languages**. You should see the heading
   **Languages** and a table of the languages of the site, the main language first.
3. Under **Add a language**, in **Language to add**, choose the language, for example **Spanish (es)**. You can type
   the first letters of its name to move through the list.
4. Choose **Add language**. You should see the message "Added Spanish. Translate pages into it from each page’s
   editor." and Spanish in the table.

Pages in the **main language** have addresses without a language part, such as `/about`. Pages in the other languages
start with the language code in lower case, such as `/es/about`.

chunks.page: Add a language and translate a page
chunks.heading: Start with the ready-made pages
chunks.text:
New websites come with six starter pages (home, About, Contact, Privacy, Terms and Accessibility). To get them in the
new language too:

1. On the **Languages** screen, choose **Create the starter pages in Spanish**.
2. Each starter page gets a Spanish translation, as a **draft**. Nothing is published until you publish each
   translation (see below).

When SightPress has no ready-made text in that language, the drafts are written in British English for you to
translate, and a message says so.

chunks.page: Add a language and translate a page
chunks.heading: Translate a page
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Pages** in the admin menu, then the page, for example **About us**.
2. In the page editor, go to the **Translations** section. It lists each language of the site with the state of the
   page in it: *Not written yet*, *Draft*, *Draft translation*, *Published*, or *Drafted by the AI assistant, not
   checked yet*.
3. Next to Spanish, choose **Translate into Spanish from British English**. This copies the title, address and
   blocks into a new Spanish draft and opens it. The British English page doesn't change.
4. Translate the title, the address (for example `sobre-nosotros`), the summary and every block, then choose
   **Save page**.

!!! tip "Let the AI assistant draft it"

    If the AI assistant is on, **Draft a translation into Spanish with the AI assistant** writes a first draft for
    you, block by block. It is marked *Drafted by the AI assistant, not checked yet* until a person saves a change or
    chooses **I checked this translation**, and can't be published before that. See
    [Use the AI assistant](use-the-ai-assistant.md).

chunks.page: Add a language and translate a page
chunks.heading: Publish the translation
chunks.text:
1. In the Spanish translation's editor, choose **Publish this translation**. The same checks run as for any page:
   for example, every picture needs a description in Spanish.
2. If a check fails, a list at the top says what to fix. Fix it, save, and publish again.
3. You should see the message "Published the Spanish translation. Visitors can see it now." and **Published** next
   to Spanish in the **Translations** section.

Visitors see a translation only when both the page and the translation are published. A draft translation is not
in the menus, the sitemap or the language links that search engines read.

chunks.page: Add a language and translate a page
chunks.heading: Check it on the website
chunks.text:
1. Go to the page in its new language, for example <http://localhost:8080/es/sobre-nosotros>.
2. You should see the page in Spanish. The menus use the Spanish titles, and the language switcher lists each
   language in its own words, such as "Español".
3. Someone whose browser asks for a language when they open the home page is taken to the home page in that
   language, or the closest one: for example Brazilian Portuguese to European Portuguese, and otherwise the main
   language.

Pictures can have their description, caption and transcript in each language: open the picture in **Media** and
fill in the fields for each language. When a language has none, the main language's text is used, never nothing.

chunks.page: Add a language and translate a page
chunks.heading: Change the main language or remove a language
chunks.text:
- **Make Spanish the main language** changes the addresses of the pages in the old and the new main language. Links
  to their old addresses stop working, so do this early, before the website is public.
- **Remove Spanish** asks you to confirm on its own page. The Spanish translations are **kept** but can't be read.
  Adding Spanish again brings them back. People who chose Spanish for their emails get the main language instead.

chunks.heading: With the command line tool
chunks.text:
In the `skeleton` folder, replace `demo` with the short name of your website:

```sh
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:locale:add demo es
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:locale:default demo es
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:locale:remove demo es --yes
```

Without `--yes`, `site:locale:remove` only explains what would happen. To start a website in several languages, give
`site:create` a list, such as `--locale=en-GB,pt-PT,es`: every starter page is then written in each of them.

A **module** is an extra package that gives SightPress new features, for example events, a shop or a booking form.
Once it is installed, each website's admins decide whether to use it: a module is a feature like the others on the
*Features* screen (see [Turn features on or off](turn-features-on-or-off.md)).

Installing and removing modules is done by whoever runs your SightPress installation, on the server. Turning a module
on or off for a website is done by one of its **admins**.

!!! note "No module is installed from the admin panel"

    For safety, modules are never uploaded through the website. They are installed on the server with Composer, the
    same way as SightPress itself and its themes.

chunks.heading: Before you start
chunks.text:
- You need the name of the module's package, for example `acme/events`.
- The package must say which versions of `sightpress/module-interface` it works with. SightPress checks that when it
  starts. A module that doesn't fit your version is listed as unavailable, with the reason, and the websites keep
  working.

chunks.heading: Install a module
chunks.text:
Run these in your project folder. With Docker, put `docker compose run --rm --no-deps php` in front of each one, as in
[Try the command line tool](try-the-command-line-tool.md).

1. Install the package: `composer require acme/events`.
2. Check that SightPress found it: `bin/sightpress site:module:list demo`, with the short name of one of your
   websites instead of `demo`. You should see a line for the module, for example `acme.events`, that says it is
   **off**.

A module you install is **off for every website that already exists**: nothing changes on them until an admin turns it
on. Websites you create afterwards start with the module's own choice, on or off, unless `config/tenant.php` says
otherwise (see [Choose for every website](#choose-for-every-website)).

chunks.heading: Turn it on for a website
chunks.text:
An admin of the website does it:

1. Sign in to the admin panel and choose **Features** in the admin menu.
2. Find the module and choose **Turn on** followed by its name.
3. The message says it is on. SightPress has prepared the website's database for it, and the roles that should use it
   can now do so: admins always, and the roles the module names (for example editors).
4. Check: the module's screens are in the admin menu, and its public pages, if it has any, are on the website and in
   its sitemap.

Or, in a terminal: `bin/sightpress site:module:enable demo acme.events`.

To give the module's permissions to other roles, see [Create a custom role](create-a-custom-role.md): a module's
permissions are listed on the role screens with the others while the module is on.

chunks.heading: Turn it off
chunks.text:
On the *Features* screen, choose **Turn off** followed by its name, and confirm. Its pages and screens are gone and
its data is kept, so turning it on again brings everything back. You can also delete its data for good: see
[Turn features on or off](turn-features-on-or-off.md#delete-a-features-data).

Or: `bin/sightpress site:module:disable demo acme.events` (add `--purge-data` to delete its data too).

chunks.heading: Remove a module
chunks.text:
1. Turn it off on every website that uses it (see above). Delete its data first if you won't need it again: once the
   package is removed, SightPress can't do that for you.
2. Remove the package: `composer remove acme/events`.
3. Check: `bin/sightpress site:module:list demo` no longer shows it.

If you remove a module that a website still had **on**, that website keeps working without it, and its data stays in
the website's database. Its admins see the module under **Features that were removed**, which says to ask whoever runs
the server to install it again to bring it back.

chunks.heading: When a module can't be used
Choose for every website
chunks.text:
In `config/tenant.php`, the `modules` section works for modules as for every other feature: `defaults` chooses what
new websites start with, and `locked` turns a module on or off for every website. See
[Turn features on or off](turn-features-on-or-off.md#for-whoever-runs-the-installation) and the
[tenant configuration reference](../reference/tenant-config.md).

To build a module of your own, follow the [Create a module](../tutorials/create-a-module.md) tutorial. The
[module interface reference](../reference/module-interface.md) lists everything a module can use.

**Captions** show the words and important sounds of a video as it plays. A **transcript** gives the same information
as text that anyone can read, including people using a screen reader or a braille display. SightPress asks for them
before a page with a video or recording can be published.

chunks.heading: Add captions to a video
chunks.text:
Captions are a WebVTT file, with a name ending in `.vtt`. Many video and subtitle tools can export one.

1. In the admin menu, choose **Media**, then open the video.
2. Find the **Captions** heading. There is one file field per language of the website.
3. Choose the file under **Captions file in …**, then choose **Upload captions in …**.
4. You should see "The captions have been saved." If the file has a mistake, it is refused with the line to fix, for
   example "line 3: the cue must end after it starts".

Visitors get a captions choice per language in the video player. It starts on the language of the page, or else the
website's main language.

chunks.heading: Write a transcript
chunks.text:
1. In **Media**, open the video or recording.
2. Write the transcript for each language. Include who is speaking and any important sounds.
3. Choose **Save details**.

Visitors open it with the **Transcript** button under the player, by mouse or keyboard. Transcripts of public files
are also in each page's Markdown version and in `llms-full.txt`, for AI readers.

!!! note "A video with no speech"

    A video with no speech still needs a description of what happens in its transcript.

chunks.heading: Tidy a transcript with the AI assistant
chunks.text:
If the [AI assistant](use-the-ai-assistant.md) is on, it can add punctuation, paragraphs and speaker labels to a saved
transcript of up to 6,000 characters. It can't change the words: an answer that does is refused.

1. Choose **Tidy up the transcript**, then **Insert**.
2. Read the result against the recording, and correct it.
3. Tick **I checked the transcript against the recording**, then choose **Save details**.

Until someone has checked it, pages that show it can't be published.

chunks.heading: Privacy
chunks.text: Captions and transcripts can name or quote people. They are deleted with the file.

When a website has [text messages](set-up-text-messages.md) on, you can add your mobile number to your account. It is
up to you: you need it only to get notifications by text, to [sign in with your phone](sign-in-with-your-phone.md)
and, on websites that ask for it, to [confirm important changes](confirm-important-changes.md).

chunks.heading: Add it
chunks.text:
1. Sign in. If you have no number yet, the website asks **Add your mobile number** straight away. You can choose
   **Skip for now** and add it later from **My account → Mobile number and text messages**.
2. Choose your **Country**, then type your **Mobile number** the way you usually write it, for example
   `07700 900123`. A number that starts with `+` and the country code works too.
3. Choose **Send the code**. The website checks it is a mobile number, then sends you a text with a 6-digit code.
   The text never contains a link.
4. Type the code in **6-digit code** and choose **Confirm my number**. You should see "Your mobile number is now …".

If the website says it isn't a mobile number, check that you didn't type a landline. If the provider didn't answer in
time, try again in a minute.

chunks.heading: Choose your text messages
chunks.text:
Having a number signs you up for nothing. On the same page, tick **Send me text messages**, choose which ones you
want, and choose **Save my choices**. Untick it to stop them, or reply STOP to any of our texts.

chunks.heading: Change or remove it
chunks.text:
On **My account → Mobile number and text messages**, type a new number to change it (the old one stops working at
once, also for signing in), or choose **Remove my number**.

A port is a numbered door on your computer that a program listens on. Each address SightPress uses ends in a port
number, such as the `8080` in `http://localhost:8080`. If another program already uses one of these ports,
SightPress can't start and you see an error such as "port is already allocated". This guide shows you how to
choose different ports.

chunks.heading: The ports SightPress uses
chunks.text:
| Setting              | Default | What it is for                              |
|----------------------|---------|---------------------------------------------|
| `HTTP_PORT`          | 8080    | SightPress itself                           |
| `MAILPIT_UI_PORT`    | 8025    | The test e-mail inbox                       |
| `MAILPIT_SMTP_PORT`  | 1025    | Where the test e-mail inbox receives e-mail |
| `MINIO_API_PORT`     | 9000    | File storage                                |
| `MINIO_CONSOLE_PORT` | 9001    | The file storage console                    |

The error message names the port that is taken, for example `127.0.0.1:8080`.

chunks.heading: Change a port
chunks.text:
1. If SightPress is running, stop it. See [Run SightPress in the background](run-in-the-background.md#stop-sightpress),
   or press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> in the terminal where it runs.
2. In the `skeleton` folder, check whether a file called `.env` exists. If it doesn't, create it by copying the
   example file:

    ```sh
    cp .env.example .env
    ```

    On Windows in PowerShell, `cp` works too.

3. Open `.env` in a text editor, such as Notepad on Windows or TextEdit on macOS. The name starts with a dot, so
   some file browsers hide it; you can open it from the editor's **Open** menu instead.
4. Find the line for the port you want to change, for example `HTTP_PORT=8080`, and change the number, for
   example to `HTTP_PORT=8081`. Pick a number between 1024 and 65535 that no other program uses.
5. Save the file.
6. Start SightPress again with `docker compose up`.
7. Use the new number in the address. With `HTTP_PORT=8081`, go to <http://localhost:8081>. You should see the
   **No site configured** page.

chunks.heading: Who can reach these ports
chunks.text:
Every port listens only on your own computer (the address `127.0.0.1`, also called `localhost`). Other computers on
your network can't reach SightPress.

chunks.page: Change your email address or password
chunks.text: Everyone with an account on a website, members included, can change their own details on **My account**.

chunks.page: Change your email address or password
chunks.heading: Open My account
chunks.text:
Sign in, then choose **My account**: in the admin panel it is a link in the header; on the website, go to `/account`,
for example <http://localhost:8080/account>.

On *My account* you can also change your name, display name, time zone, language (on websites in several languages)
and profile picture. People who use the admin panel can choose **Reduce motion** and **Larger text** there.

chunks.page: Change your email address or password
chunks.heading: Change your password
chunks.text:
1. On *My account*, choose **Change your password**.
2. In **Current password**, type the password you use now.
3. In **New password**, type a new one. The rules are written under the field.
4. Choose **Change password**. You should see "Your password has been changed. You are still signed in here, and
   signed out everywhere else."

If the current password is wrong, a message at the top of the page says so. After five wrong tries in 15 minutes,
you have to wait, as when signing in.

chunks.page: Change your email address or password
chunks.heading: Change your email address
chunks.text:
1. On *My account*, choose **Change your email address**.
2. Type the **New email address** and your **Current password**, then choose **Send the code**.
3. We email a 6-digit code to the **new** address. The email has no link.
4. Type the code on the next page and choose **Confirm my new email address**. You should see "Your email address is
   now …. Sign in with it from now on."

Your old address gets an email saying that the address was changed, with the new one partly hidden and no link.
Until you type the code, nothing changes. See [Codes we send you](codes-we-send-you.md).

Every change is written to the website's audit log, without the passwords.

A **layout** decides how a page's content is arranged. You choose one for each page. Your words and blocks stay the
same when you change it.

1. In the admin menu, choose **Pages**, then open a page, or choose to add a new one.
2. Find **Layout** and choose one.
3. Save the page, then open it to check how it reads.

| Layout | What it does | Good for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Home page** | The title and summary as a large introduction. | The first page of the website. |
| **Standard page** | One comfortable reading column. | Most pages. |
| **Landing** | A wide introduction band, then content in full-width sections. | A single campaign or call to action. |
| **Sidebar** | Content with a side column of related links and notes. It lists the pages in the same section. | A section with several related pages. |
| **Full width** | Content across the whole page width. | Wide galleries and tables. |

On narrow screens and when zoomed in, every layout becomes one column, so nothing needs sideways scrolling.

chunks.heading: When you change theme
chunks.text:
Not every theme has every layout. Before you switch to a theme that lacks one, the **Appearance** screen lists the
pages affected. They are shown in the standard layout, and they keep their own layout for when you switch back. See
[Install and change a theme](install-and-change-a-theme.md).

This guide helps whoever runs a SightPress installation decide how large a file each website accepts. A brochure
website might keep small pictures and no large videos, while a podcast needs long audio files.

chunks.heading: The two kinds of limit
chunks.text:
- **Website limits** say how large a picture, video, audio file or document can be. Each website can have its own.
- **Server limits** say how much the server takes in one upload. They are the same for every website. If you need to
  change them, see [Fix upload size limits](fix-upload-size-limits.md).

People can upload the **smaller** of the two. Website admins see the result in **Site settings** and next to each
upload field, but they can't change it.

chunks.heading: Recommended values
chunks.text:
| Kind of installation       | `UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE` | `PHP_MEMORY_LIMIT` | Website limits                                                    |
|----------------------------|-------------------|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Standard** (the default) | `64M`             | `256M`             | Pictures 20 MB, documents 50 MB, audio 200 MB, video 1 GB         |
| **Small or shared hosting** | `32M`            | `256M`             | Pictures 20 MB, documents 20 MB, audio and video 32 MB            |
| **Lots of media**          | `64M`             | `512M` | Larger audio and video, and pictures up to 50 million pixels |

With JavaScript, SightPress [sends large files in parts](upload-large-files.md), so a file can be larger than
`UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE`, up to the website's limit. Without JavaScript, a file can't be larger than `UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE`.

chunks.heading: See a website's limits
chunks.text:
Type this in the `skeleton` folder, replacing `demo` with the website's short name:

```sh
docker compose exec php bin/sightpress site:media:limits demo
```

You should see each kind of file, its limit, and whether it is **this site**'s own value or the **install default**.

chunks.heading: Change a website's limits
chunks.text:
1. Lowering a limit needs no preparation. To **raise** one above the default, first set the most any website may
   use in `config/tenant.php`:

    ```php
    'media' => [
        'limits' => [
            'max' => ['audio' => '500M'],
        ],
    ],
    ```

2. Set the website's limit:

    ```sh
    docker compose exec php bin/sightpress site:media:limits demo --audio=500M
    ```

    You should see **The upload limits of "demo" have been saved.** A value above the maximum is refused, and the
    message says what the maximum is.

3. Find out which server values that limit needs:

    ```sh
    docker compose exec php bin/sightpress system:check --site=demo --recommend
    ```

    It prints lines ready to copy into `.env`, or into the settings of PHP, nginx, Apache or Caddy. Leave out
    `--site=demo` to get the values that suit all your websites.

4. If the values differ from yours, change them and restart, as in
   [Fix upload size limits](fix-upload-size-limits.md).

To go back to the installation's limits:

```sh
docker compose exec php bin/sightpress site:media:limits demo --reset
```

chunks.heading: Check what the web server really accepts
chunks.text:
SightPress can't read the web server's limit, so it can test it by sending empty files of growing sizes. Nothing is
stored. In the standard Docker setup:

```sh
docker compose exec php bin/sightpress system:check --probe-url=http://nginx
```

You should see a line such as **Probe: the web server accepts 65 MB and refuses 66 MB.** If that is less than
SightPress was told, the command says which setting to correct.

chunks.heading: If something goes wrong
chunks.text:
**"The audio limit of 600 MB is above the most this install allows"**
:   Raise `max` in `config/tenant.php` (step 1), or choose a lower value.

**The new limit doesn't show on the upload form**
:   The server's limit is probably lower. Run the command in step 3 and change the values it prints.

**"The probe got the answer 404"**
:   The address doesn't reach this SightPress. In Docker, use `http://nginx` and run the command with
    `docker compose exec php`.

A SightPress website **never sends you a link** to click. When it needs to check that an e-mail address or a mobile
number is yours, it sends a **6-digit code** instead, and you type that code on the website yourself.

This keeps you safe from fake messages. If you ever get a message that claims to come from a SightPress website and
asks you to click a link, it is not from us. Don't click it.

chunks.heading: When you get a code
chunks.text:
You get a code by e-mail when:

- you **forgot your password** and asked for a new one: the code works for 15 minutes;
- someone **invited you** to help with a website: the invitation code works for 7 days.

On websites with [text messages](set-up-text-messages.md), you get a code **by text message** when:

- you [add or change your mobile number](add-your-mobile-number.md): the code works for 10 minutes;
- you [reset your password with your number](sign-in-with-your-phone.md): 10 minutes;
- the website [asks you to confirm an important change](confirm-important-changes.md): 10 minutes.

A text with a code says which website it is from, for example "123 456 is your code for Riverside Library. It works
for 10 minutes. Never share it." It never contains a link or a web address.

The person who sets up a new website gets a **setup code** from the command line tool, not by e-mail. They pass it
on to the website's first admin, who uses it to choose a password. A setup code works for 7 days.

Each code works only once.

chunks.heading: What a code message looks like
chunks.text:
- The subject names the website, for example "Your code to reset your password for Riverside Library" or "Ada
  invited you to Riverside Library". The code itself is never in the subject.
- The message has the code on its own line, for example `123 456`.
- The message has no links, no web addresses and no pictures.
- It ends with: "We will never send you a link. Type this code on the page where you asked for it. Never share it
  with anyone."

chunks.heading: Type a code
chunks.text:
1. Go to the page that asked for the code. For a password, that is the page you are already on. For an invitation,
   go to the website's sign-in page and choose **Accept an invitation**.
2. Find the field called **6-digit code**.
3. Type the 6 digits. You can type them with or without the space in the middle.
4. Choose **Continue**. The page never sends the code by itself, so take your time.
5. You should see the next step, for example a page where you choose your password.

chunks.heading: If the code doesn't work
chunks.text:
- Check the digits and try again. After 5 wrong tries the code stops working.
- A code also stops working when it is too old, when it has been used, or when you asked for a newer one.
- On the password page, choose **Send a new code**. You can ask for a new code once a minute; if it is too soon,
  the page tells you how many seconds to wait.
- For an invitation, ask the person who invited you to invite you again.
- For a setup code, ask the person who set up the website for a new one.

chunks.heading: Try it on your computer
chunks.text:
When SightPress runs on your computer, the e-mails with codes go to the test inbox. See
[Open the test e-mail inbox](open-the-test-email-inbox.md).

A website can ask for a **code by text message** before important changes, so a stolen password alone can't change
who runs it. This is called two-step confirmation. It needs [text messages](set-up-text-messages.md).

chunks.heading: What counts as important
chunks.text:
Changing your password, email address or mobile number; inviting an admin or editor; changing someone's role or
deactivating them; editing roles; who can read the website and who may sign up; security settings; turning features
on or off; the AI assistant's key; cloud storage; deleting analytics data.

chunks.heading: Turn it on (admins)
chunks.text:
1. [Add your own mobile number](add-your-mobile-number.md) first. Without it you can't confirm anything.
2. Go to **Site settings → Security**.
3. Choose **On: important changes need a code sent by text message** and **Save**.
4. Choose **Send me a code**, type the code from the text, then **Make the change**. You should see "Two-step
   confirmation is on."

Your organisation may have decided for every website: then the page says so and has no switch.

chunks.heading: Make an important change
chunks.text:
1. Make the change as usual, for example change your email address.
2. You see **Confirm it's you**. Nothing has changed yet.
3. Choose **Send me a code**, type the 6-digit code from the text, and choose **Confirm**.
4. Choose **Make the change**. For a change that needs your password, choose **Go back to the form** and type it
   again: passwords are never kept.

For the next 10 minutes, in the same browser, other important changes don't need another code.

If you have no mobile number yet, the website asks you to add one first. There is no way round it by email.

chunks.heading: If no code comes
chunks.text:
- Wait a minute and choose **Send a new code**.
- If you replied STOP to our texts before, reply **START** to our last text.
- If the page says it can't send a code right now, ask whoever runs your websites: they can make the change for you
  from the command line.

Lost your phone? See [Lost your phone](lost-your-phone.md).

A **role** is a set of things people may do on your website. Everyone has one role. Every website starts with four:
**Admin** (everything), **Editor**, **Contributor** and **Member** (reads members-only pages, nothing more). You can
change Editor and Contributor, and make your own roles, for example "Shop staff" who may upload pictures and change
the menus but not publish pages.

You need to be an **admin**, or have a role that may **Manage roles**.

chunks.heading: Create a role
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Roles** in the admin menu. You see every role, how many permissions it has and how many people have it.
2. Choose **Create a role**.
3. In **Name of the role**, type a name people will understand, for example `Shop staff`.
4. Tick what people with this role may do. The permissions are grouped by area (Pages, Media, Menus, People …), and
   each one says what it allows. For example, under **Media** tick **Upload media**, and under **Menus** tick
   **Manage menus**.
5. Choose **Create role**. You should see "Created the role “Shop staff”."

A role with any permission can also open the admin panel: **Use the admin panel** is added for you.

chunks.heading: Give the role to someone
chunks.text:
1. Choose **People** in the admin menu, then the person's name.
2. Under **Change role**, choose your new role and then **Change role**. You should see, for example, "Cleo’s role is
   now Shop staff."

The change applies from their next click.

chunks.heading: Change or delete a role
chunks.text:
- Open the role from **Roles**, change its name or the ticked boxes, and choose **Save role**.
- To delete it, choose **Delete this role** at the bottom of its page. A role that someone still has can't be
  deleted: give those people another role first.

chunks.heading: What you can't do
chunks.text:
These rules keep your website safe. If you try, the page tells you why, next to the box or name concerned, and keeps
what you ticked:

- **Admin** and **Member** can't be changed, renamed or deleted.
- The role people get when they [sign up](let-people-sign-up.md) can only have permissions that are safe for people
  you don't know, such as writing pages and sending them for review.
- You can't take **Manage roles** away from your own role, so you can't lock yourself out. Ask another admin.
- Features that are [turned off](turn-features-on-or-off.md) don't show their permissions. A role keeps them, so
  they come back when you turn the feature on again.

Every change to a role is written to the **Audit log**, under **Roles**.

chunks.heading: On the command line
chunks.text:
The same rules apply on the [command line](try-the-command-line-tool.md), where a website is named by its slug:

```bash
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:role:list demo
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:role:create demo shop_staff --label="Shop staff" --permissions=media.upload,menu.manage
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:role:grant demo shop_staff page.create
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:role:revoke demo shop_staff page.create
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:role:delete demo shop_staff
```

One SightPress installation can run many websites. Each website has its own pages, people, files and settings,
kept in its own database. This guide shows you how to create a website with the command line tool, and what each
part of the command means.

Before you start, follow [Getting started](../getting-started.md) up to step 6, so that SightPress runs and has a
secret key.

chunks.heading: Create the website, answering questions
chunks.text:
The easiest way is to let the command ask you everything, one question at a time.

1. Open a terminal and go to the `skeleton` folder.
2. Type:

    ```sh
    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:create
    ```

3. Answer each question and press Enter. Each question says what to type. When it ends with "Press Enter for"
   and a value, pressing Enter without typing takes that value. When it lists choices, such as "Type person or
   organization", type one of them; capital letters don't matter.
4. For the database, the command first asks which engine to use. Press Enter for **SQLite**: it keeps the
   website in one file and needs nothing else. Press Enter again to keep the file in the `sites` folder. If you
   choose MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL instead, the command asks for the server, port, database name, user name and
   password one by one, each with a usual value you can keep with Enter. The password isn't shown as you type it,
   and you type it twice so a typing mistake is caught.
5. For the main language, type a code such as `en-GB` or `pt-BR`. Capital letters don't matter and you can use
   `_` instead of `-`. The command says the language in words, for example "That is Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR).
   Is that right?". Type `yes` or press Enter if it is, or `no` to type it again.
6. If an answer isn't right, for example an e-mail address without the part after `@`, the command says what is
   wrong and asks again. After 3 wrong answers in a row i

chunks.heading: Create the website with one command
chunks.text:
If you already know every answer, for example in a script, give them all on one line. The command then asks
nothing. This example creates a website called "Riverside Library" for an organisation:

```sh
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:create demo --domain=localhost --db-engine=sqlite --url=http://localhost:8080 --owner-type=organization --locale=en-GB --name="Riverside Library" --admin-email=ada@example.org --admin-first-name=Ada --admin-last-name=Lovelace
```

If something is wrong, the command says what, and creates nothing.

chunks.heading: What each part means
chunks.text:
| Part | What to give | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `demo` | A short name for the website: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. You use it in other commands. | `library` |
| `--domain` | The web addresses of the website, without `https://`, separated by commas. Each address belongs to one website only. On your own computer, use `localhost`. | `library.example.org,www.library.example.org` |
| `--db-engine` | The database engine: `sqlite`, `mysql`, `mariadb` or `postgresql`. On your own computer, SQLite is simplest. See [Start a database server](start-a-database.md) for the others. | `sqlite` |
| `--db-path` | For SQLite: the file. Optional: without it, a file named after the short name in the `sites` folder. | `library.sqlite` |
| `--db-host`, `--db-port`, `--db-name`, `--db-user`, `--db-password` | For the other engines: the server, its port, the database, and the user name and password. Without them, `localhost`, the engine's usual port, `sightpress_` and the short name, `sightpress` and no password. | `--db-host=db --db-user=library` |
| `--db` | Instead of the parts above: the whole database address in one go. | `sqlite:////app/sites/library.sqlite` |
| `--owner-type` | Who runs the website: `organization` or `person`, in capitals or not. The ready-made pages say "we" for an organisation and "I" for a person. | `person` |
| `--locale` | The website's main language. Capital letters don't matter, and `_` works as well as `-`. | `en-GB`, `pt_br`, `fr-FR` |
| `--name` |

chunks.heading: What a new website has
Try SightPress with demo content
chunks.text:
Add `--with-demo-content` to the command to fill the new website with examples:

- five files in the media library: a picture, a short video with captions, a sound recording and a PDF;
- a page called "Every kind of block" at `/every-block`, with one block of every kind, and a page under it;
- three more people, each waiting for their setup code: Bea Okafor (editor), Cleo Martins (contributor) and Max
  Müller (member).

The command prints a setup code for each person. The `example.org` addresses can't receive e-mail, so give the codes
to whoever tries the website out.

chunks.heading: Give someone a new setup code
chunks.text:
A setup code works once, for 7 days. To make a new one for an admin who hasn't chosen a password yet, type:

```sh
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:user:create-admin demo --email=ada@example.org --first-name=Ada --last-name=Lovelace --url=http://localhost:8080
```

You should see a new setup code. The old one stops working. The same command adds another admin when you give a new
e-mail address. Someone who already has a password uses **Forgot your password?** on the sign-in page instead.

chunks.heading: Turn a website off, or remove it
chunks.text:
| To | Type | Visitors see |
| --- | --- | --- |
| turn it off for a while | `bin/sightpress site:disable demo` | "temporarily unavailable" |
| turn it on again | `bin/sightpress site:enable demo` | the website |
| close it and keep its data | `bin/sightpress site:archive demo` | "gone" |
| delete it, softly | `bin/sightpress site:delete demo` | "not found"; the data is kept |
| remove a deleted website for good | `bin/sightpress site:purge demo` | — |

Start each command with `docker compose run --rm --no-deps php`, as above. `site:purge` keeps the database unless
you add `--drop-database`, which can't be undone. The [command line reference](../reference/command-line.md) lists
every command.

How large a file you can upload depends on two things: what the website accepts for each kind of file, and what the
server accepts in one go. This guide explains the warning admins see when the server's settings are too low, and
how to change them.

chunks.heading: What you see
chunks.text:
- Next to the upload field in **Media**, everyone sees the largest file they can upload, for example "Largest file
  you can upload: pictures 20 MB, documents 50 MB, audio files 200 MB and videos 1 GB." Large files are
  [sent in parts](upload-large-files.md). Without JavaScript the lower server limit applies, and the hint says so.
- If you choose a file that is too large, the browser refuses it before sending it. The reason appears under the
  field, which gets focus, so screen readers read it out.
- If something too large is sent anyway, you see a page called **This is too large to send**. It says how much the
  server accepts and has a **Go back to the form** link.
- Admins see a warning called **Your server’s settings stop some uploads** on the dashboard and in **Media**. Each
  point names a server setting and the value it needs. It also says how many uploads the web server refused in the
  last 7 days. Editors and contributors don't see it.
- To put the warning away, choose **Hide until this changes**. It comes back by itself if the result changes.

chunks.heading: Change the limits on your own computer
chunks.text:
With SightPress running in Docker, the limits are one group of lines in the `.env` file of the `skeleton` folder.
PHP and the web server both read them, so they always match.

1. If there is no `.env` file in the `skeleton` folder yet, create it by copying the example:

    ```sh
    cp .env.example .env
    ```

2. Open `.env` in a text editor and find the lines that start with `UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE`.
3. Change the values you need:

    | Setting            | Recommended | What it is                                                      |
    |--------------------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
    | `UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE`  | `64M`       | The largest file in one upload                                  |
    | `INPUT_MAX_SIZE`   | `8M`        | The largest form without files, such as a long page             |
    | `INPUT_MAX_VARS`   | `5000`      | How many fields one form can have; lower values can lose content |
    | `MAX_FILE_UPLOADS` | `20`        | How many files one upload can hold                               |
    | `PHP_MEMORY_LIMIT` | `256M`      | Memory for one request; `512M` for pictures over 25 million pixels |
    | `UPLOAD_TIMEOUT`   | `300`       | Seconds a slow upload may take                                   |

    Sizes are whole megabytes or gigabytes, such as `64M` or `1G`. On a small site or shared hosting, `32M` is
    enough for `UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE`.

4. Save the file and restart SightPress:

    ```sh

chunks.heading: On a hosting provider's server
chunks.text:
If someone else runs your server, send them the warning's text. It names the settings, for example
`upload_max_filesize`, `post_max_size` or the web server's limit (`client_max_body_size` for nginx), and the value
each needs. Ask them to tell you when it is done, then open the dashboard again: the warning is gone once the
settings are right.

chunks.heading: Choose how large each website's files can be
chunks.text: To give one website larger or smaller limits than the others, see [Choose upload limits](choose-upload-limits.md).

chunks.heading: Large audio files and videos
chunks.text:
The website accepts audio files up to 200 MB and videos up to 1 GB. With JavaScript, SightPress
[sends large files in parts](upload-large-files.md), so they can be larger than `UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE`. Without JavaScript,
one upload can't be larger than `UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE`. `system:check` mentions this lower limit as a note, not a problem.

If you have many files, or files too large for the browser, you can add them to a website's media library from the
server. This is done by whoever runs your SightPress installation. Website limits on file size don't apply, but every
safety check does.

Start each command with `docker compose run --rm --no-deps php`, as in
[Try the command line tool](try-the-command-line-tool.md). The folder must be one the command can read: with Docker,
put it inside the `skeleton` folder.

1. Import a folder into the website `demo`, including the folders inside it:

    ```sh
    bin/sightpress site:media:import demo imports/ --recursive
    ```

2. Read the result. Each file gets a line, then a summary such as `Imported: 12. Already present: 1. Refused: 1.`
3. Open **Media** in the admin panel. New files are unpublished until you describe and publish them.

chunks.heading: Options
chunks.text:
| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--recursive` | Also imports the files inside folders. |
| `--publish` | Publishes the new files straight away. |
| `--alt="…"` | Gives every new picture this description. Use it only if it is true of all of them. |
| `--locale=pt-PT` | The language of that description. The default is the website's main language. |
| `--memory-limit=2G` | Gives this run more memory, for very large pictures. |

chunks.heading: What happens to each file
chunks.text:
- **Imported:** the file passed the checks and is in the library.
- **Already present:** the library already has exactly this file, so it isn't stored twice.
- **Refused:** the line says why, for example that a file isn't really the type its name says. The import carries on
  with the other files, and the command ends with an error so that scripts notice.

A very large picture is refused with the memory it needs. Run the command again with `--memory-limit=` and that value.

A **theme** decides how your websites look: colours, fonts, spacing and the layout of the pages. Every SightPress
installation has the **default theme**, and you can install more. Each website then uses one of the installed
themes, and you can change it at any time. Your pages and their content stay the same: only the look changes.

Installing a theme is done by whoever runs your SightPress installation, on the server. Choosing a theme for a
website is done by one of its **admins**.

!!! note "No theme is installed from the admin panel"

    For safety, themes are never uploaded through the website. They are installed on the server, the same way as
    SightPress itself.

chunks.heading: Install a theme
chunks.text:
You need the name of the theme's package, for example `acme/theme-harbour`. Run these in your project folder. With Docker,
put `docker compose run --rm --no-deps php` in front of each one, as in
[Try the command line tool](try-the-command-line-tool.md):

1. Install the package: `composer require acme/theme-harbour`.
2. Let SightPress notice it: `bin/sightpress cache:clear`.
3. Check it: `bin/sightpress theme:validate acme-harbour`. You should see "The theme … passes". If it fails, the
   message says what is wrong, for example a colour pair that is too hard to read, with the colours and the ratio.
   A theme that fails can't be used until its author fixes it.
4. See every theme: `bin/sightpress theme:list`. Each line shows the theme, its version, whether websites may use it,
   and which websites use it.

chunks.heading: Choose which themes websites may use
chunks.text:
By default, every installed theme can be used by every website, and new websites start with the default theme. To
change that, edit `config/tenant.php`:

```php
'themes' => [
    // Only these themes can be chosen; null means every installed theme.
    'allowed' => ['default', 'acme-harbour'],
    // The theme of new websites. It must be one of the allowed themes.
    'default' => 'acme-harbour',
],
```

If the default theme isn't one of the allowed themes, SightPress won't start and says why.

chunks.heading: Change the theme of a website
chunks.text:
In the admin panel (you need to be an admin of the website):

1. In the admin menu, choose **Appearance**.
2. You should see one section for each installed theme, with its name as a heading, what it is like, and its
   **Status** in words, for example "The site's theme" or "Available". If a picture of the theme was made, it is
   there with a description; otherwise the description is written out.
3. To look first, choose **Preview …** (it opens in a new tab): a sample page with every kind of block in that theme.
4. Choose **Use …**. If some pages use a layout the theme doesn't have, a page lists them first: they will be shown
   in the standard layout, and they keep their own layout for later. Choose **Use …** again to go ahead, or
   **Keep the current theme**.
5. A message at the top says the theme is now the site's theme. Screen readers read the message out.

Or from the command line: `bin/sightpress site:theme:apply demo acme-harbour` (the website's short name, then the
theme). SightPress checks the theme again before it applies it, and the website's activity log records the change.

Open the website: it now has the new look. The other websites keep theirs.

chunks.heading: Change the colours of the theme
chunks.text:
1. On the **Appearance** screen, choose **Change the colours of the site's theme**.
2. You should see two groups, **Light mode** and **Dark mode**, each with the background, text, links, buttons and
   highlights, text on buttons, borders and the focus outline. Each colour is written as `#` and six digits or
   letters, for example `#0a57c2`.
3. Change a colour and choose **Save the colours**.
4. If the colour is too hard to read against the colours next to it, SightPress refuses it and says which colours
   clash and by how much, for example "on-primary on primary has a contrast of 2.14:1 in light mode; it needs at
   least 4.5:1". What you typed is kept, so you can adjust it.
5. To undo your changes, choose **Use the theme's own colours**.

The admin panel keeps its own colours whatever you choose.

chunks.heading: Choose a layout for each page
chunks.text:
Themes offer layouts such as **Landing**, **Sidebar** and **Full width**. See
[Choose a page layout](choose-a-page-layout.md).

chunks.heading: Pictures of each theme
chunks.text:
The pictures and previews on the **Appearance** screen are made on the server by
`bin/sightpress theme:publish-assets`, which runs after every `composer install` and `composer update`. Pictures
need Node.js and the Chromium browser on the server; without them, the screen describes each theme in words and
still links to its preview.

chunks.heading: Remove a theme
chunks.text:
1. Run `bin/sightpress theme:list` to see which websites use the theme.
2. Give those websites another theme first (see above).
3. Remove the package: `composer remove acme/theme-harbour`, then `bin/sightpress cache:clear`.

If a website still used the theme, nothing breaks: the website is shown in the default theme. Its admins see
"Your site is shown in the default theme" on the dashboard, with the reason, and the server log notes it too.
Choosing a theme for the website again makes the message go away.

chunks.heading: The admin panel keeps its look
chunks.text:
The admin panel always uses the look of the default theme, whatever theme a website has. Admins can always find
their way around, and the admin panel keeps its contrast.

chunks.page: Keep your files in the cloud
chunks.text:
By default, a website keeps its pictures, videos and other files on your server. You can move them to **cloud
storage** instead, and let a **CDN** (content delivery network) deliver public files from near each visitor. Both are
optional. Nothing is sent to another company unless you set it up.

This is done by whoever runs your SightPress installation, with the command line tool. Start each command with
`docker compose run --rm --no-deps php`, as in [Try the command line tool](try-the-command-line-tool.md). The examples
use a website called `demo`.

!!! warning "Before you start"

    - **It may cost money.** AWS and Cloudflare charge for storage and traffic. Check their prices first.
    - **Your files move to another company.** Files can contain personal data, so say so in your privacy notice. If
      the location is outside your country, that may be an international transfer of personal data.
    - **Keep a copy** of the `sites` folder until you have checked the website.

chunks.page: Keep your files in the cloud
chunks.heading: Which service to use
chunks.text:
SightPress works with any S3-compatible service, such as AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, DigitalOcean Spaces or MinIO.

SightPress can create what you need at **AWS** or **Cloudflare**. For another service, create a private bucket in its
control panel and go to [Connect the bucket](#connect-the-bucket).

chunks.page: Keep your files in the cloud
chunks.heading: Create the bucket and CDN
chunks.text:
1. Put your provider's keys in the environment for this one run. SightPress never saves them.
    - AWS: `SIGHTPRESS_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `SIGHTPRESS_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`.
    - Cloudflare: `SIGHTPRESS_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `SIGHTPRESS_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`. To use your own domain with
      `--domain`, also set `SIGHTPRESS_CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID`.
2. Read the plan. This contacts nobody and changes nothing:

    ```sh
    bin/sightpress site:storage:provision demo --provider=aws --dry-run
    ```

    You should see each item that will be created and its location.
3. Run the same command without `--dry-run` to create them. It is safe to run it twice.

**What is created.** At AWS: a private bucket, a CloudFront CDN that alone can read it, permission for browsers to
upload to it from your website, and rules that clear unfinished uploads. At Cloudflare: an R2 bucket with the same
upload permission and rules, and a public address if you use `--domain`.

**Where it is created.** The location follows the website's time zone:

| Website's time zone | AWS | Cloudflare R2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| United Kingdom | London (`eu-west-2`) | EU, because R2 has no UK location |
| EU, EEA or Switzerland | Frankfurt (`eu-central-1`) | EU |
| Anywhere else | You choose with `--region` | You choose with `--region` (`eu`, `us` or `default`) |

Creating these doesn't change your website yet.

To let the website's admins do this under **Site settings**, then **File storage**, set
`SIGHTPRESS_PR

chunks.page: Keep your files in the cloud
chunks.heading: Connect the bucket
chunks.text:
1. Create keys limited to this bucket in your provider's control panel, and set them as `SIGHTPRESS_S3_ACCESS_KEY` and
   `SIGHTPRESS_S3_SECRET_KEY`. SightPress stores them encrypted.
2. Connect the bucket. For a provider other than AWS, add its address with `--endpoint`. MinIO also needs
   `--path-style`.

    ```sh
    bin/sightpress site:storage:s3 demo --bucket=my-bucket --region=eu-west-2
    ```

    You should see that the bucket works and has been saved. The website still uses its local files.

chunks.page: Keep your files in the cloud
chunks.heading: Move the files
chunks.text:
```sh
bin/sightpress site:storage:migrate demo
```

SightPress copies each file, checks it arrived intact, and then switches the website. If it stops, run it again and it
goes on from where it was. Your local copies stay until you are sure. To delete them after the check, run the command
again with `--delete-source`. This can't be undone.

Open the website and check that its pictures and files appear.

chunks.page: Keep your files in the cloud
chunks.heading: Turn on the CDN
chunks.text:
1. Set the CDN to fetch from your website, forward its host name, include the query string in its cache key, and not
   forward cookies.
2. Turn it on, with an address that starts with `https://`, and publish the theme's files:

    ```sh
    bin/sightpress site:storage:cdn demo --url=https://cdn.example.org
    bin/sightpress theme:publish-assets
    ```

To stop using it, run `bin/sightpress site:storage:cdn demo --remove`.

Private files stay protected. Unpublished files and every file of a members-only website use signed addresses that
stop working after a short time. After you unpublish a file or make a website members-only, a copy on the CDN can last
up to five minutes.

chunks.page: Keep your files in the cloud
chunks.heading: Check it
chunks.text:
Website admins can see where files are kept under **Site settings**, then **File storage**: the provider, the bucket,
the region and the CDN address. Keys are never shown.

chunks.page: Keep your files in the cloud
chunks.heading: If something goes wrong
chunks.text:
**The command says the bucket can't be reached or the keys are wrong**
:   Nothing was changed. Check the bucket name, the region, the address and the keys, then run it again.

**Large uploads say they're using the server instead**
:   The bucket doesn't allow uploads from your website's address. Files still upload, through your server. Add your
    website's address to the bucket's CORS rules, allowing `PUT` and exposing `ETag`.

**A website is deleted**
:   `site:purge` also removes that website's folder in the bucket.

If your organisation runs SightPress for its own teams, you can make sure every website uses one of your domains,
that only people with your email addresses join, and let your colleagues register on members-only websites without
an invitation.

These settings apply to **every website** of your SightPress installation, so whoever runs it sets them in
`config/tenant.php`. Nothing changes until you set them. Admins of each website can only turn registration with an
organisation email address **off** for their own website.

chunks.heading: Websites only on your domain
chunks.text:
Add to `config/tenant.php`:

```php
'domain_policy' => ['subdomain_of' => 'example.org'],
```

From then on, [Create a website](create-a-site.md) only accepts `example.org` or a name under it, such as
`news.example.org`. A name like `evil-example.org` or `example.org.other.test` is refused, with a message saying
which names are allowed.

chunks.heading: Only your email addresses join
chunks.text:
```php
'email_policy' => ['domains' => ['example.org', 'example.com']],
```

Only addresses at exactly these domains can be invited, accept an invitation, [sign up](let-people-sign-up.md),
change to a new address in **My account**, or be the first admin of a new website. `ada@mail.example.org` only
counts if you list `mail.example.org` too. Capital letters don't matter, and international names such as
`bücher.example` work.

chunks.heading: Let colleagues register on members-only websites
chunks.text:
```php
'email_policy' => ['domains' => ['example.org', 'example.com']],
'domain_registration' => 'on',
```

`'on'` uses every domain of `email_policy`. To use only some, write `['domains' => ['example.org']]` instead.

On every [members-only website](make-a-site-members-only.md), the sign-in page now shows **Register with your
organisation email**, even while **Let anyone create an account** is off. To try it:

1. Open a private browser window and go to the sign-in page of a members-only website.
2. Choose **Register with your organisation email**. The page says which addresses can register.
3. Fill in the form with an address at one of your domains and choose **Create my account**. An address elsewhere is
   refused, and the message names your domains.
4. Type the 6-digit code from the email (see [Codes we send you](codes-we-send-you.md)). The account can't sign in
   before that.
5. Sign in. The new account has the website's sign-up role, **Member** unless an admin chose another safe one.

Public websites, and websites where anyone can already sign up, are not affected. The **Audit log** says these
accounts registered with an organisation email address.

chunks.heading: Turn it off for one website
chunks.text:
Admins of a members-only website choose **Site settings**, then **Change who can sign up**. Under **Registration with
an organisation email address**, choose **Off for this site**, then **Save sign-up settings**. The link disappears
from the sign-in page. You can also create a website with it off:

```bash
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:create … --domain-registration=off
```

chunks.heading: After you make a policy stricter
chunks.text:
Nothing is removed: websites keep answering on their domains, and people keep signing in with the addresses they
have. The policy applies to new websites, new people and changed addresses. To see what is outside it, run:

```bash
docker compose exec php bin/sightpress system:check
```

It prints a note for each website with a domain outside `domain_policy`, and how many accounts of each website have
an address outside `email_policy`.

If a setting is written wrongly, SightPress doesn't start and says what to fix, for example
`Tenant setting "domain_registration" is 'on', which uses the domains of "email_policy", but "email_policy" is 'any'.`

By default only people you invite can have an account on your website. You can also let anyone create their own
account. They confirm their email address with a 6-digit code before they can sign in.

You need to be an **admin**.

chunks.heading: Turn sign-up on
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Site settings** in the admin menu, then **Change who can sign up**.
2. Tick **Let anyone create an account**.
3. In **Role of people who sign up**, keep **Member** unless you have a reason to change it. Members can read
   members-only pages and nothing more. Only roles that are safe to give to people you don't know are listed: never
   editor or admin.
4. Choose **Save sign-up settings**. You should see "The sign-up settings have been saved."

The sign-in page now shows "New here?" with a **Create an account** link.

chunks.heading: Try it as a new person
chunks.text:
1. Sign out, or open a private browser window, and go to the sign-in page, for example
   <http://localhost:8080/login>.
2. Choose **Create an account**. Fill in your first name, last name, an optional display name, your email address,
   your time zone (your browser's is already chosen) and a password. On a website in several languages, choose your
   language too.
3. Choose **Create my account**. You should see the heading **Confirm your email address**.
4. Open the email. While you try SightPress on your computer, it is in the test inbox: see
   [Open the test e-mail inbox](open-the-test-email-inbox.md). It has a 6-digit code and **no link**.
5. Type the code in **6-digit code** and choose **Confirm my email address**. You should see "Your email address is
   confirmed and your account is ready."
6. Sign in with your email address and password.

The code works once, for 15 minutes. **Send a new code** sends another one, at most once a minute. See
[Codes we send you](codes-we-send-you.md).

chunks.heading: What keeps it safe
chunks.text:
- An account can't sign in until its email address is confirmed. Accounts that are never confirmed are removed after
  a week.
- If someone signs up with an address that already has an account, the page looks exactly the same, so nobody can find
  out who has an account. The owner of the address gets an email saying someone tried, with no link.
- A hidden field catches most automated sign-ups, and each place can send at most 10 sign-up forms an hour. There are
  no picture puzzles.
- Every new account and every change to these settings is written to the **Audit log**.

On a members-only website, your organisation may also let people with its email addresses register while sign-up is
off: see [Keep websites to your organisation](keep-websites-to-your-organisation.md).

To turn sign-up off again, untick **Let anyone create an account**. Accounts that were already made are kept.
If you lost your phone or changed your number, you can't get codes to your old number. Here is how to get going again.

chunks.heading: You can still sign in
chunks.text:
Sign in with your **email address** and password. To reset a forgotten password, choose **Forgot your password?** and
use your email address: the code comes by email.

chunks.heading: Ask for your number to be removed
chunks.text:
While the website [asks for a code for important changes](confirm-important-changes.md), you can't change your number
yourself, because that needs a code to the old one. Ask someone who manages people on the website:

1. They go to **People** and choose you.
2. They choose **Remove the mobile number of …** (they confirm it's them with their own code).

If nobody on the website can, whoever runs your websites can do it from the command line:

```sh
bin/sightpress site:user:phone:reset riverside ada@example.org
```

chunks.heading: Add your new number
chunks.text:
On **My account → Mobile number and text messages**, add your new number and type the code we send to it (see
[Add your mobile number](add-your-mobile-number.md)). Adding a first number never needs a code to an old one.

chunks.page: Make a website or a page members-only
chunks.text:
A **members-only** page can only be read by people who have an account on the website and are signed in. You can
make a single page members-only, or the whole website.

You need to be an **admin** to change the whole website, and an **editor** or **admin** to change a page.

chunks.page: Make a website or a page members-only
chunks.heading: Make one page members-only
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Pages** in the admin menu, then the page.
2. In **About the page**, under **Who can read this page**, choose **Members only: people with an account on the
   site, once they sign in**.
3. Choose **Save page**.
4. Check: sign out, or open a private browser window, and go to the page. You should see the sign-in page. After
   signing in, you are taken back to the page.

A members-only page is left out of search engines, the sitemap, `llms.txt` and site search for visitors who aren't
signed in. In the menus, it only appears for people who are signed in.

To show a menu entry only to members, for example a link to a members' forum, choose **Menus**, then **Change** next
to the entry, and tick **Only show this entry to members who are signed in**.

chunks.page: Make a website or a page members-only
chunks.heading: Make the whole website members-only
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Site settings** in the admin menu.
2. Under **Who can read the site**, choose **Only people with an account, once they sign in. Search engines and AI
   services can’t read any page.**
3. Choose **Save settings**. You should see "The settings have been saved."
4. Check: in a private browser window, go to any page of the website. You should see the sign-in page with the
   message "This site is for its members. Sign in to read it."

On a members-only website:

- People who aren't signed in can still sign in, create an account (if you let them, see
  [Let people sign up](let-people-sign-up.md)), reset a forgotten password and accept an invitation.
- Search engines and AI services can't read anything: the sitemap and `llms.txt` are empty, and every page asks not
  to be listed.
