- Every signed-in person, whatever their role, can read every published page.

chunks.page: Make a website or a page members-only
chunks.heading: Who can read what
chunks.text:
| | Visitors who aren't signed in | Members (signed in) | Editors and admins |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pages for everyone, on a public website | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Members-only pages | No: asked to sign in | Yes | Yes |
| Any page of a members-only website | No: asked to sign in | Yes | Yes |
| Drafts, older versions, archived pages | No | No | Yes |
| The admin panel | No | No | Yes |

To give people accounts, invite them from **Invite someone** in the admin menu, or let them sign up themselves.

chunks.page: Move or rename a page without breaking links
chunks.text:
When a published page gets a new address, or moves somewhere else on the website, SightPress remembers its old
address. Anyone who follows an old link or bookmark is taken to the new address, and search engines are told that the
page has moved for good. You don't need to do anything for this to happen.

You need to be an **editor** or **admin**.

chunks.page: Move or rename a page without breaking links
chunks.heading: Give a page a new address
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Pages** in the admin menu, then the page.
2. In **Address**, type the new last part of the address, for example `opening-times` instead of `hours`. Use
   lower-case letters, digits and hyphens.
3. Choose **Save page**.
4. Check: open the old address, for example <http://localhost:8080/hours>. You should land on
   <http://localhost:8080/opening-times>.

Pages under it move with it: `/hours/holidays` becomes `/opening-times/holidays`, and its old address leads there
too.

chunks.page: Move or rename a page without breaking links
chunks.heading: Move a page somewhere else on the website
chunks.text:
In the page editor, the **Place in the site** section has these buttons:

- **Move up** and **Move down** change the order of pages at the same level, for example in a menu of pages.
- **Move under the page before it** puts the page one level down, under the page just above it.
- **Move out to the level above** puts the page one level up.
- **Move to**: choose **The top level of the site** or any other page in the list, then choose **Move the page**.

After each move, a message says where the page is now, and focus stays in the section. Pages under it move with it,
and every old address leads to the new one.

chunks.page: Move or rename a page without breaking links
chunks.heading: See and change the redirects
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Redirects** in the admin menu. You should see the table **Old addresses and where they lead**, with each
   **Old address**, its **Language** and where it **Leads to**. A page that was deleted for good shows "Gone: the
   page was deleted".
2. To stop an old address leading anywhere, choose **Remove the redirect from** followed by that address.
3. To add your own, for example for a page from an old website, fill in **Old address** (such as `/old-news`) and
   **New address** (such as `/news`) under **Add a redirect**, then choose **Add redirect**. The new address must be
   in the same language.

A few rules keep this tidy:

- If a page moves twice, its oldest address leads straight to the newest one, never through a chain.
- A redirect that would go round in a circle is refused.
- A new page that uses an old address wins: the redirect stops and visitors see the new page.

The **Pages not found** report on the *Analytics* screen lists addresses people asked for that don't exist, with a
link to add a redirect for each. See [See who visits your website](see-who-visits-your-website.md).

SightPress comes with a file storage program called MinIO, which has its own web console. This guide shows you how
to sign in to it.

1. Start SightPress (see [Getting started](../getting-started.md)).
2. In your web browser, go to <http://localhost:9001>.
3. You should see the MinIO sign-in page.
4. Sign in with the user name `sightpress` and the password `sightpress-secret`.
5. You should see the MinIO console. There are no files yet.

By default, each website keeps its uploaded files, such as pictures and documents, in its own folder inside the
`sites` folder of the `skeleton`, so MinIO stays empty. The `site:storage:s3` command can move
a website's storage to MinIO or another S3-compatible service.

If you changed `MINIO_ROOT_USER`, `MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD` or `MINIO_CONSOLE_PORT` in your `.env` file, use your
values instead. These settings only take effect the first time the storage starts.

When SightPress runs on your computer, it never sends real e-mail. Every message goes to a test inbox called
Mailpit instead, so you can read it without anything leaving your computer. This guide shows you how to open it.

1. Start SightPress (see [Getting started](../getting-started.md)).
2. In your web browser, go to <http://localhost:8025>.
3. You should see the Mailpit inbox. It is empty for now, with a message saying there are no messages.

SightPress sends e-mail when:

- someone forgets their password and asks for a code;
- someone is invited to help with a website;
- a page is sent for review: every editor and admin is told;
- a visitor sends a message with a contact form.

Each of these messages appears here a moment later. Choose a message to read it.

The inbox only gets messages when your `.env` file has the line `MAILER_DSN=smtp://mailpit:1025`. The file you copied
from `.env.example` in [Getting started](../getting-started.md) already has it. Without it, SightPress sends nothing.

If you changed `MAILPIT_UI_PORT` in your `.env` file, use that number instead of `8025`.

This guide helps you decide how to set up a SightPress website before you build it. Answer a few questions about what
the website needs. The guide then suggests the settings to choose and the content to write.

You don't need to be technical to do the planning. Some choices are made by whoever runs your SightPress installation,
and this guide says which ones.

!!! note "Which version this guide describes"

    This guide describes version 0.5. If you run 0.4, update first: it has no modules from others, custom roles,
    email or domain policies, text messages or two-step confirmation. See [Update SightPress](update-sightpress.md).

chunks.heading: Step 1: Answer these questions
chunks.text:
Write down your answers. Each one points to a choice in the next steps.

| Question | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Who is the website for, and what must they be able to do? | Decides your pages and calls to action. |
| Is it public, or only for members? | Decides who can read it and whether search engines can find it. |
| Who will write, check and publish pages? | Decides the roles you give people. |
| Which languages do you need? | Decides how much translation to plan for. |
| Will you publish large videos, audio or many files? | Decides file storage and upload limits. |
| Do you expect a few visitors or a lot? | Decides the database and whether you need a CDN. |
| Will you run one website or several? | Decides what to set for every website and what to set for each one. |
| Do you want visitor figures, an AI assistant or features from other modules? | Decides which optional features to turn on. |
| Should only people from your organisation join? | Decides the email policy and whether colleagues can register themselves. |
| Will people want texts, or to sign in with their phone? | Decides whether to set up text messages, and their cost. |

chunks.heading: Step 2: Start from the closest kind of website
chunks.text:
Pick the row closest to yours. You can change every choice later.

| Kind of website | Database | Files | Access | People | Features |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Personal website or portfolio | SQLite | On the server | Public | One admin | Search off if there are few pages |
| Small business | SQLite | On the server | Public | One admin, perhaps an editor | Search and analytics |
| Charity or community group | SQLite or MariaDB | On the server | Public, with some members-only pages | Admin, editor, volunteer contributors | Search and analytics |
| Podcast or media project | MariaDB or PostgreSQL | Cloud storage and a CDN | Public | Admin and editors | Search and analytics |
| School, library or museum | MariaDB or PostgreSQL | Server, or cloud storage if there is a lot of media | Public | Web editor, staff as contributors | Search and analytics |
| Public service or health information | MariaDB or PostgreSQL | Server or cloud storage | Public | Editors approve every page | Search, and analytics if your policy allows it |
| Private club or staff website | SQLite or MariaDB | On the server | Members-only, perhaps with colleagues registering by work email | Admin, editors, members | Search |
| Agency or group of websites | MariaDB or PostgreSQL | Cloud storage per website | Set per website | Separate people per website | Defaults set for all websites |

chunks.heading: Database
chunks.text:
Each website has its own database. You choose it when you [create the website](create-a-site.md).

| Choose | When |
| --- | --- |
| **SQLite** | One small or medium website on one server. It is a single file and needs nothing else. |
| **MariaDB or MySQL** | Several people edit at once, the website is busy, or your host already provides it. |
| **PostgreSQL** | Your organisation already uses it, or the website is large and busy. |

You can move later, but SightPress doesn't copy the data for you. See `site:db:change` in the
[command line reference](../reference/command-line.md).

chunks.heading: File storage
chunks.text:
| Choose | When |
| --- | --- |
| **On the server** (the default) | Pictures and documents, and a server with enough disk space. |
| **Cloud storage** | Lots of media, large files, or more than one server. Works with AWS, Cloudflare and other S3-compatible services. |
| **Cloud storage with a CDN** | Visitors in many countries, or popular audio and video. A CDN delivers public files from near each visitor. |

Whoever runs the installation sets up cloud storage with the command line tool. This example uses AWS in London:

```sh
bin/sightpress site:storage:provision demo --provider=aws --region=eu-west-2 --dry-run
bin/sightpress site:storage:provision demo --provider=aws --region=eu-west-2
bin/sightpress site:storage:s3 demo --bucket=your-bucket --region=eu-west-2
bin/sightpress site:storage:migrate demo
bin/sightpress site:storage:cdn demo --url=https://files.example.org
```

- The first command only shows the plan. It creates nothing and contacts nobody.
- The second needs your provider's keys in the server's environment: `SIGHTPRESS_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and
  `SIGHTPRESS_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. For Cloudflare, use `--provider=cloudflare` with
  `SIGHTPRESS_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `SIGHTPRESS_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`.
- The third needs keys limited to this bucket, in `SIGHTPRESS_S3_ACCESS_KEY` and `SIGHTPRESS_S3_SECRET_KEY`. For a
  provider other than AWS, also give its address with `--endpoint`.
- The website keeps using its current files until `site:storage:migrate` has copi

chunks.heading: Upload limits
chunks.text:
| Kind of website | Suggested setup |
| --- | --- |
| Brochure website, or shared hosting | The **Small or shared hosting** values |
| Most websites | The **Standard** values, which need no change |
| Podcast, video or photography | The **Lots of media** values, with higher audio and video limits for that website |

[Choose upload limits](choose-upload-limits.md) gives the exact values. To add many files at once, or very large ones,
use `site:media:import`, which applies the same safety checks.

chunks.heading: Who can read and join
chunks.text:
- **Public** is the default. Search engines and AI services can find the pages.
- **Some pages for members** suits reports or resources for a group. See
  [Make a website or a page members-only](make-a-site-members-only.md).
- **The whole website for members** hides every page from search engines and AI services.
- **Open sign-up** suits communities. Keep new people as **Member**. See [Let people sign up](let-people-sign-up.md).
- **Invitation only** is the default, and suits most teams and private websites.
- **Only your organisation's email addresses** can be set for every website by whoever runs the installation. On
  members-only websites, colleagues can then register with their work email without an invitation. See
  [Keep websites to your organisation](keep-websites-to-your-organisation.md).

chunks.heading: Roles
chunks.text:
Give each person the lowest role that lets them do their work. Try to have at least two people who can publish, so
that someone can cover absences.

| Role | Give it to |
| --- | --- |
| **Admin** | The one or two people responsible for the website. |
| **Editor** | People who check and publish pages. |
| **Contributor** | People who write, such as volunteers or staff, whose pages need approval. |
| **Member** | People who only read members-only pages. |

If none fits, [create a custom role](create-a-custom-role.md) with exactly the permissions someone needs, such as an
"Events editor". See [Roles and permissions](../reference/roles-and-permissions.md).

chunks.heading: Text messages and two-step confirmation
chunks.text:
Text messages are off until whoever runs the installation sets up a provider (Twilio or Vonage). Each message costs
money, so set a monthly budget.

| Use | Good for | Think about |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Notifications by text](text-message-notifications.md) | Editors who need to know at once when a page waits for review. | People choose it themselves, and can reply STOP. |
| [Sign in with your phone](sign-in-with-your-phone.md) | People who find a mobile number easier than an email address. | Only verified numbers work. |
| [Confirm important changes](confirm-important-changes.md) | Any website where a wrong change would do harm, such as giving someone the admin role. | Everyone who makes such changes needs a mobile number. |

A mobile number is personal data: say why you ask for it in your privacy notice. See
[Set up text messages](set-up-text-messages.md).

chunks.heading: Languages
chunks.text:
Choose one main language, then add others only when someone can keep them up to date. A page without a translation is
better than an old one. The admin panel is available in British English, Spanish and European Portuguese, and a website
can publish in other languages. See [Add a language](add-a-language.md).

chunks.heading: Look and layout
chunks.text:
Start with the default theme. You can install other themes and change the colours on the
**Appearance** screen, and SightPress checks that they stay readable. Choose a layout for each page:

| Layout | Good for |
| --- | --- |
| **Home page** | The first page, with a large introduction. |
| **Standard page** | Most pages. |
| **Landing** | A single campaign or call to action. |
| **Sidebar** | A section with several related pages. |
| **Full width** | Wide galleries and tables. |

See [Choose a page layout](choose-a-page-layout.md) and [Install and change a theme](install-and-change-a-theme.md).

chunks.heading: Optional features
chunks.text:
| Feature | New websites | Turn it on when | Think about |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Site search](search-your-website.md) | On | The website has more than a handful of pages. | Leave private or duplicate pages out of the search. |
| [Analytics](see-who-visits-your-website.md) | On | You will act on the figures. | You can keep them for 1 to 25 months. |
| [AI assistant](use-the-ai-assistant.md) | Off | You want help drafting, and have an API key and a budget. | Check where the service processes data. A person checks every suggestion. |
| [Modules from others](add-a-module.md) | Off | You need a feature SightPress doesn't have, such as events. | Install only modules you trust, and turn each one on only where it is needed. |

If you run several websites, set the defaults for all of them in `config/tenant.php`. See
[Turn features on or off](turn-features-on-or-off.md).

chunks.heading: Search engines and AI services
chunks.text:
In **Site settings**, under **Search & AI**, choose whether AI services may read your pages:

- **Allow all** suits most websites that want to be found.
- **AI search only** lets AI assistants link to you, and asks crawlers that train AI models to stay out.
- **Block all** asks every AI crawler to stay out.

See [Search and AI visibility](../reference/search-and-ai.md).

chunks.heading: Step 4: Plan your content
chunks.text:
Every new website starts with a home page, About, Contact, a privacy notice, terms of use and an accessibility
statement. These are starting points. **Read and rewrite each one**, especially the privacy notice and terms, so they
are true for your organisation.

| Kind of website | Suggested pages | Most useful blocks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Personal website | Home, About me, Projects, CV, Contact | Text, Image, File download |
| Portfolio | Home, Work, one page per project, About, Commissions | Gallery, Columns, Video, Contact form |
| Small business | Home, What we offer, Prices, About us, Find us, Contact | Call to action, Gallery, Contact form |
| Charity or community group | Home, What we do, Get involved, Donate or volunteer, Annual reports, Contact | Call to action, Video, File download, List of pages |
| Podcast or media project | Home, Episodes, one page per episode, Guests, About | Audio with a transcript, File download |
| School, library or museum | Home, Visit us, Opening hours, What's on, Accessibility, Policies, Contact | Video, Audio, File download, Video or map from another site |
| Public service or health information | Home, one page per service, How to apply, Forms, Accessibility, Contact | Heading, Text, File download, Sign language video |
| Private club or staff website | Home, News, Guides, Documents, People, Contact | Text, File download |

For every website, plan to:

- write one clear purpose for each page, and put the most important thing first;
- u

chunks.heading: Step 5: Check before you launch
chunks.text:
- [ ] The name, logo, contact details and time zone are right in **Site settings**.
- [ ] Every ready-made page has been read and rewritten.
- [ ] The contact form reaches the right person.
- [ ] Each person has the right role, and at least two people can publish.
- [ ] Every page passes the accessibility checks.
- [ ] You have tried the main tasks with a keyboard alone, and with a screen reader if you can.
- [ ] `site:seo:check` reports no duplicate titles.
- [ ] Whoever runs the installation has a copy of the `sites` folder, the databases and `APP_SECRET`.
- [ ] Someone is responsible for updates, and has read [Update SightPress](update-sightpress.md).

chunks.heading: What to plan around today
chunks.text:
SightPress doesn't do the following yet. If your website depends on one of them, plan another way or wait.

- **A guide for a public server.** Getting started covers your own computer. Have someone experienced set up HTTPS,
  backups and updates.
- **Several web servers.** Sign-in sessions are kept in files, so servers must share them, and share the upload folder.
- **Shops and payments, event booking, or a blog with an RSS feed.** Podcasts can publish episodes as pages, but
  SightPress doesn't produce a podcast feed.
- **Tools to download or delete someone's personal data.** If privacy law applies to you, such as UK or EU GDPR, plan
  how you will answer these requests.

chunks.heading: Where to go next
chunks.text:
1. Follow [Getting started](../getting-started.md) to run SightPress.
2. [Create your website](create-a-site.md) with the choices you made.
3. [Write and publish your first page](write-and-publish-a-page.md).

chunks.page: Put a page in the trash and get it back
chunks.text:
You can take a page off the website in two ways, and both keep it so you can bring it back:

- **Archive** keeps the page out of sight. Visitors who open its address are told the page isn't found.
- **Put in the trash** is for pages you want to get rid of. Visitors who open its address are told the page is
  **gone**, so search engines drop it. A page stays in the trash until someone deletes it for good.

You need to be an **editor** or **admin**.

chunks.page: Put a page in the trash and get it back
chunks.heading: Archive a page
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Pages** in the admin menu, then the page.
2. Choose **Archive**. You should see "Archived. Visitors can’t see the page any more; it is kept with the archived
   pages."
3. To bring it back, open it again and choose **Restore as a draft**. It comes back as a draft: publish it again when
   it is ready.

chunks.page: Put a page in the trash and get it back
chunks.heading: Put a page in the trash
chunks.text:
1. Open the page in the editor.
2. Choose **Put in the trash**. You should see "Put in the trash. Its address now tells visitors the page is gone."

A page with pages under it can only go in the trash once those pages are in the trash already, so nothing is left
without a page above it.

chunks.page: Put a page in the trash and get it back
chunks.heading: Find a page in the trash and get it back
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Pages** in the admin menu.
2. In the **State** filter, choose **In the trash**, then choose **Show pages**. You should see only the pages in the trash.
3. Open the page and choose **Take out of the trash**. You should see "Restored as a draft. Publish it again when it
   is ready."

A page comes out of the trash as a draft, and only when the page above it isn't in the trash.

chunks.page: Put a page in the trash and get it back
chunks.heading: Delete a page for good
chunks.text:
This can't be undone.

1. Open a page that is in the trash.
2. Choose **Delete this page for good**. A page asks you to confirm, and lists what goes with it: the pages under it,
   every translation and every older version.
3. Choose **Delete for good** to go ahead, or **Keep it in the trash** to go back.

Its address then tells visitors and search engines that the page is gone, until a new page uses the address. Menu
entries that pointed to it are removed.

chunks.page: Put a page in the trash and get it back
chunks.heading: Copy a page
chunks.text:
**Copy this page** makes a new draft right after the page, in every language it is written in, titled "Copy of …",
with `-copy` added to its address. The pages under it aren't copied. The copy opens in the editor.

Every step on this page is written to the website’s audit log, which admins can read.

If something in SightPress doesn't work, shows an error, or stops you from doing something with your keyboard,
screen reader, zoom or colour settings, please tell us. You don't need to know which part of SightPress is at fault.

chunks.heading: What to tell us
chunks.text:
Whichever way you report it, these help us most:

1. What you were trying to do, for example "publish a page in Spanish".
2. What happened. Copy any error message as text.
3. What you expected to happen.
4. The SightPress version, if you know it, and your browser and operating system.
5. For an **accessibility barrier**: your assistive technology and its version, if you use one, and what was
   announced or what happened.

Accessibility barriers are always treated as bugs, never as feature requests.

chunks.heading: Report it by email (no GitHub account needed)
chunks.text:
1. Write an email to <contribute@sightpress.org>, in any format that suits you: text, a voice recording or a
   document. Write in your own words; imperfect English is welcome.
2. A maintainer replies within 5 working days, adds the report to GitHub for you, and tells you what happens next.

chunks.heading: Report it on GitHub
chunks.text:
If you have a GitHub account:

1. Go to [open an issue in SightPress core](https://github.com/sightpress/core/issues/new/choose). If the problem is
   in this documentation, use [the docs issues](https://github.com/sightpress/docs/issues/new/choose) instead; if you
   aren't sure, use core and we'll move it.
2. Choose **Report a problem**, or **Report an accessibility barrier**. Each form says which fields are required, in
   words.
3. Fill in the form and choose **Submit new issue**.

A maintainer replies, asks for anything that is missing and labels the issue.

chunks.heading: Security problems
chunks.text:
Never report a security problem in public. Email <security@sightpress.org>, or use **Report a vulnerability** on the
*Security* tab of the repository on GitHub. We acknowledge every report within 5 working days.

chunks.heading: Problems with people
chunks.text:
To report behaviour that breaks the
[Code of Conduct](https://github.com/sightpress/docs/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md), email
<conduct@sightpress.org>. Reports are confidential.

chunks.page: Restore an older version of a page
chunks.text:
Every time a page is saved, SightPress keeps a version of it. You can see who saved each version and when, read what
changed, word by word, and bring an older version back. Restoring never publishes anything.

You need to be able to change the page: a **contributor** for your own drafts, or an **editor** or **admin**.

chunks.page: Restore an older version of a page
chunks.heading: See the older versions
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Pages** in the admin menu, then the page.
2. Next to the page's state, choose **Older versions**. You should see a table of versions, newest first: the
   version number, when it was saved (in your own time zone), who saved it, and the state the page was in then.
   "The system" means a change made from the command line or on a schedule.

On a website in several languages, each translation has its own versions. Links at the top of the screen lead to the
versions in each language.

chunks.page: Restore an older version of a page
chunks.heading: See what changed
chunks.text:
1. Choose a version number, for example **Version 3**. You should see what changed since the version before it: first
   the details of the page (title, address, summary, search fields), then each block, under a heading that says
   whether it was changed, added, removed or has no changes.
2. Inside a field, words that were taken out read "[removed: …]" and are crossed out; words that were put in read
   "[added: …]" and are underlined.

The words "removed" and "added" are always written out, so the comparison reads the same with a screen reader, in
high contrast mode and without colours.

chunks.page: Restore an older version of a page
chunks.heading: Bring a version back
chunks.text:
1. On the version's screen, choose **Restore version 3** (with that version's number).
2. You should see "Restored version 3 as version 5. Nothing was published: the page is still a draft." The newer
   versions stay in the list, so you can change your mind.

Restoring brings back the title, address, search fields and blocks. It doesn't change the layout, who can read the
page or its place on the website.

**While the page is published, restoring is refused**, because visitors would see the old text straight away. Choose
**Unpublish** first (or make that translation a draft), restore the version, check it, and publish again.

A version with a block that no longer exists can't be restored: copy what you need from it instead.

When someone changes a theme, for example the default theme's colours or the layout of its pages, the change arrives
as a pull request on GitHub. You can see exactly what it looks like without installing anything: every theme pull
request comes with a preview you download and open in your browser. You don't need to know anything about code.

chunks.heading: Find the preview
chunks.text:
1. Open the pull request on GitHub.
2. Find the comment titled **Theme preview**, near the top of the conversation. A new change to the pull request
   updates the same comment; it never adds another one.
3. The comment says, in words, what the theme looks like, and how many accessibility problems the automatic check
   found in light mode, dark mode and forced colours (Windows contrast themes). "No violations" in all three is the
   goal.
4. Select **Download the preview**. GitHub asks you to sign in first; the download is a zip file and is kept for 30
   days.

chunks.heading: Open it
What to check
chunks.text:
Go through the page as you would for [Review the interface](review-the-interface.md):

1. **Contrast.** Is any text, link, button or border hard to see? Switch your computer or browser to dark mode and
   look again, and try a contrast theme on Windows.
2. **Focus.** Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> again and again. Can you always see where you are?
3. **Zoom and small screens.** Zoom to 200% and 400%, and make the window very narrow. Is anything cut off, on top of
   something else, or only readable by scrolling sideways?
4. **The description.** Does the description in the comment match what you see? It is what people who can't see
   the screenshots get instead, so it must be right.
5. **The change itself.** The pull request says what it changes. Does the page show that, and nothing else?

chunks.heading: Describe what you see

chunks.text:
SightPress is led by blind people. Sighted reviewers help us check what is hard to check without sight. You don't
need to know anything about design or code: if something looks wrong to you, it probably is.

chunks.heading: What to check
chunks.text:
Go through a few screens of the admin panel and of a website (see [Getting started](../getting-started.md) to run
your own) and look for these:

1. **Contrast.** Is any text, icon or border hard to see? Check in light mode, in dark mode, and with a high
   contrast theme (on Windows, *Settings → Accessibility → Contrast themes*).
2. **Focus.** Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> again and again. Can you always see where you are?
3. **Zoom.** Zoom the browser to 200% and to 400% (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> and <kbd>+</kbd>, or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> and
   <kbd>+</kbd> on a Mac). Is any text cut off or on top of other text? Do you have to scroll sideways to read a line?
4. **Small screens.** Make the window very narrow, about the width of a small phone. Does everything still fit?
5. **Spacing.** Is anything squashed together or badly lined up?
6. **Pictures.** Do the icons, the generated profile pictures, the sharing images and the charts look right? Are
   the screenshots in the documentation up to date?
7. **Labels.** Does the text you see on a button or a field match what it does? A screen reader announces the same
   words, so they must make sense on their own.
8. **Colour alone.** Is any information shown only by colour, such as red for an error, without words?

chunks.heading: How to describe a screenshot
Send your review
chunks.text:
On GitHub, [open an issue](https://github.com/sightpress/core/issues/new/choose) and choose **Interface review**.
The form asks for the screen, your browser, zoom level and colour mode, what looks wrong, and a description of any
screenshot. Without a GitHub account, email the same to <contribute@sightpress.org>.

In [Getting started](../getting-started.md), SightPress runs in a terminal window and stops when you close it.
This guide shows you how to run it in the background instead.

chunks.heading: Start SightPress
chunks.text:
1. Open a terminal and go to the `skeleton` folder, for example:

    ```sh
    cd sightpress/skeleton
    ```

2. Type:

    ```sh
    docker compose up --detach --wait
    ```

3. Wait until the command finishes. You should see one line per container (`php`, `nginx`, `mailpit` and
   `minio`), each ending with `Healthy`. You get your terminal back.
4. Go to <http://localhost:8080>. You should see the **No site configured** page.

    The very first time, SightPress keeps installing for a minute or two after the command finishes, and the
    browser shows **502 Bad Gateway**. Wait a minute, then reload the page.

You can now close the terminal. SightPress keeps running until you stop it or restart your computer.

chunks.heading: See what is running
chunks.text:
Type:

```sh
docker compose ps
```

You should see a table with one row for each container. The **STATUS** column says `Up` and how long the
container has been running.

chunks.heading: Read the messages SightPress writes
chunks.text:
Type:

```sh
docker compose logs --follow
```

You see the messages from every container, and new ones as they arrive. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> to
stop reading. SightPress keeps running.

chunks.heading: Stop SightPress
chunks.text:
Type:

```sh
docker compose --profile "*" down
```

You should see lines ending with `Removed`. The `--profile "*"` part also stops a database server if you started
one. Your settings and stored files are kept for next time.

!!! tip "Shortcuts for macOS and Linux"

    If the `make` program is installed, you can type `make up` to start SightPress in the background and
    `make down` to stop it. Type `make` on its own to list every shortcut.

A page can be published at a set time, and taken off the website again at another time, without anyone being there
to press a button. This is useful for an event page that should appear on Monday morning, or a notice that should
disappear when an offer ends.

You need to be an **editor** or **admin**: people who may publish pages.

chunks.heading: Before you start
chunks.text:
SightPress does what is scheduled once a minute, with a helper called the **scheduler**. When you start SightPress
with `docker compose up` (see [Getting started](../getting-started.md)), the scheduler starts too. To see what it
does, type `docker compose logs -f scheduler` in the `skeleton` folder.

chunks.heading: Publish a page at a set time
chunks.text:
1. Write the page and take it through review until it is **Approved** (see
   [Write and publish a page](write-and-publish-a-page.md)). Only an approved page can be published on schedule.
2. In the page editor, go to the **Schedule** section. It says "Nothing is scheduled." and shows **your time zone**
   above the fields. Change your time zone on *My account* if it is wrong.
3. In **Publish at**, choose the day and time.
4. Choose **Save the schedule**. You should see a message such as "Scheduled: the page is published at 1 Dec 2026,
   09:00 (Europe/London time)."
5. In the page list, the page shows "Approved · To be published at 1 Dec 2026, 09:00".

Within a minute of that time, the page is published.

chunks.heading: Take a page off the website at a set time
chunks.text:
1. In the **Schedule** section, choose a time in **Take off the site at**.
2. Choose **Save the schedule**.

At that time the page becomes a draft again, if it is published then.

chunks.heading: Change or clear the schedule
chunks.text:
Change the times and choose **Save the schedule** again, or choose **Clear the schedule** to remove both times.
Archiving a page or putting it in the trash clears its schedule too.

chunks.heading: If something goes wrong
chunks.text:
- **A time in the past**, an end before the start, or a time that doesn't exist (the night the clocks go forward) is
  explained, and the form keeps what you typed.
- The page is published **as the person who scheduled it**: the same publish checks run. If a check fails, or that
  person may no longer publish, nothing is published, the audit log says why, and the time is cleared so that
  you can fix the page and schedule it again.
- If the computer or server was off at the time, the page is published as soon as the scheduler runs again.

Whoever runs SightPress on a server sets the scheduler up once; see the [command line reference](../reference/command-line.md#things-that-happen-at-a-set-time).

Every page of a website has a search box in its header. It finds the website's published pages in the language you
are reading, by their title, their summary and their text, including the descriptions of pictures, the transcripts
of recordings and the names of downloads. Site search is an optional feature, on by default.

chunks.heading: Search from any page
chunks.text:
1. Open any page of your website, for example `http://localhost:8080/`.
2. In the header, find **Search this site**. With a keyboard, press Tab until you reach the search box.
3. Type one or more words, for example `opening hours`, and press Enter (or choose **Search**).
4. You should see the results page. Its title and heading say what you searched for and how many results there are,
   for example "2 results for “opening hours”". Screen readers read this out when the page opens.
5. Each result has its title as a link, where it is on the website ("In: About us › Team") and a few lines of its
   text with the words you searched for in bold and underlined. Choose a title to open the page.

Good to know:

- Capitals and accents don't matter: `cafe` finds "Café".
- Words are matched by their stem: `libraries` finds "library".
- The last word can be the start of a word: `accessib` finds "accessibility".
- Pages with every word come first. When no page has every word, the results page says so and shows pages with some
  of them.
- With ten results or more, links at the bottom ("Search results pages") lead to the next pages.

chunks.heading: When nothing is found
chunks.text:
The page says "No results for …" and gives tips: check the spelling, try fewer or other words. On a website in
several languages, the language list at the top leads to the same search in the other languages.

chunks.heading: Pages for members only
chunks.text:
Pages for members only are found only by people who are signed in. Sign in, search again, and they appear in the
results.

chunks.heading: Leave a page out of the search
chunks.text:
1. Open the page in the admin panel's page editor.
2. In the **Search & AI** section, tick **Leave this page out of the site’s own search**.
3. Choose **Save**.
4. Check: searching for the page's title no longer finds it. Search engines can still list the page, unless you also
   tick **Ask search engines and AI search engines not to list this page**.

The choice is made for each language of the page.

chunks.heading: If new pages don't show up
chunks.text:
The search follows every change as it is saved. After a bigger change (adding a language, changing the website's
main language, making the whole website members-only, or turning search back on), SightPress rebuilds the search
within a minute, as long as it runs in the background (see
[Run SightPress in the background](run-in-the-background.md)). To rebuild it straight away, in the `skeleton` folder
type (replace `demo` with your website's short name):

```sh
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:search:reindex demo
```

You should see one line per language, such as `en-GB: 12 documents indexed.`

chunks.heading: Turn search off
chunks.text:
Search is a feature: an admin can turn it off on the **Features** screen (see
[Turn features on or off](turn-features-on-or-off.md)). The search box and the results page are then gone.

SightPress counts how many people visit your website, which pages they read, where they come from, what they search
for and which addresses are not found. It also shows which search engines and AI crawlers read the website.
Analytics is an optional feature, on by default.

It is private by design: visits are counted on your own server, with no cookies, no tracking scripts and nothing
sent to other companies. SightPress never stores visitors' IP addresses or details of their browser. This is not
legal advice, but it means most websites don't need a cookie banner for it.

chunks.heading: Open the Analytics screen
chunks.text:
1. Sign in to the admin panel as an admin or an editor, for example at `http://localhost:8080/admin`.
2. In the admin menu, choose **Analytics**. (Contributors don't have it.)
3. You should see the last 30 days. Under **Days to show**, the link for the range you are looking at is marked as
   the current one; choose **Last 7 days**, **Last 90 days** or **Last 12 months** to change it.
4. For other dates, fill in **First day** and **Last day** under **Other days** and choose **Show these days**. If a
   date is missing or the last day comes before the first, a box at the top says "There is a problem" and links to
   the field to fix.

Days run from midnight to midnight in your website's time zone, which the screen names, so everyone sees the same
numbers. Today's numbers are counted live.

chunks.heading: Read the numbers
chunks.text:
At the top, three sentences sum up the range, for example "1,349 visitors, up 12% on the 30 days before". The arrows
next to them are only decoration: the words say the same.

Each part of the screen has its own heading, so a screen reader can move between them:

- **Visitors over time**: a chart, with a sentence above it that says what it shows, for example "Visitors went up
  12% compared with the previous 30 days, from 1,204 to 1,349. The busiest day was Tuesday 4 November, with 98
  visitors." This period is a solid line with round markers, the period before a dashed line with square markers.
  Choose **Show the data for each day** to see every day in a table.
- **Pages read most**, **Where visitors came from** and **Devices** (phone, tablet or computer): tables, with a
  small bar next to each number.
- **Languages**: only on websites in more than one language.
- **Site search**: what people searched for, and the searches that found nothing. Only while site search is on.
  Searches that look like an email address or a phone number are counted but never shown.
- **Pages not found**: addresses people asked for that don't exist. People who can edit any page see **Add a
  redirect** next to each one: it opens the Redirects screen with the address filled in.
- **Search engines and AI crawlers**: which programs read the website and what they read. They are never counted
  as visitors.

Each part has a **Download … as a CSV file** link, for a spreadsheet. The file has every row

chunks.heading: What is counted and what isn't
chunks.text:
- A visitor is counted once per day. The same person on two days counts twice; there is no "returning visitors"
  number, on purpose.
- Not counted: people signed in to the website, visitors whose browser asks websites not to track them (Global
  Privacy Control or Do Not Track), the admin panel, pictures and other files, and pages a browser only loads in
  advance.
- Figures are kept for 25 months, so you can compare two full years.

chunks.heading: The dashboard
chunks.text:
The dashboard (`/admin`) shows **Last 7 days**: one sentence with the visitors and page views of the last week, and
a link to the Analytics screen.

chunks.heading: Keep analytics for less time, or delete them (admins)
chunks.text:
1. On the Analytics screen, go to **Keeping analytics** at the bottom.
2. In **Months to keep analytics for**, type a number from 1 to 25 and choose **Save**. Older figures are deleted
   within the hour. The change is in the audit log.
3. To delete everything, choose **Delete analytics data**. A page asks you to confirm; choose **Delete analytics
   data** again, or **Keep the data** to go back. Counting goes on from then.

chunks.heading: From the command line
chunks.text:
In the `skeleton` folder (replace `demo` with your website's short name):

```sh
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:analytics:report demo
```

You should see the visitors, page views and views per visitor of the last 30 days, each with the 30 days before.
Add `--report=pages` (or `sources`, `devices`, `not-found` …) for another report, and `--format=csv` or
`--format=json` for a file. If it warns that analytics were "last rolled up" long ago, SightPress isn't running in
the background (see [Run SightPress in the background](run-in-the-background.md)).

chunks.heading: Turn analytics off
chunks.text:
Analytics is a feature: an admin can turn it off on the **Features** screen (see
[Turn features on or off](turn-features-on-or-off.md)). Nothing is counted any more, and the figures already
counted are kept until they are deleted. If your website's **Privacy notice** page was written by SightPress, remove
its "Visitor statistics" section.

A website can send text messages (SMS): codes that check a mobile number is yours, notifications people choose, codes
to sign in or reset a password, and codes for [important changes](confirm-important-changes.md). Text messages are
**off** on every website until whoever runs your SightPress installation sets them up, because they cost money and
send phone numbers to another company.

You need a text message account at **Twilio** or **Vonage** (other providers can come as modules), and the command
line tool (see [Try the command line tool](try-the-command-line-tool.md)).

chunks.heading: 1. Choose who sends
chunks.text:
Get these from your provider's dashboard:

| Provider | Account | Key | Sender |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Twilio | Account SID (starts with `AC`) | Auth token | A number such as `+447700900123`, or a name of 3 to 11 letters and digits, such as `Riverside` |
| Vonage | API key | API secret, then `|`, then the signature secret | A number or a name |

Names as senders are not allowed in every country. Check your provider's rules for the countries you send to.

chunks.heading: 2. Give them to the website
chunks.text:
The key is read from the keyboard, never typed on the command line, so it doesn't end up in your shell history:

```sh
printf %s "$TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN" | bin/sightpress site:sms:set riverside --provider=twilio \
    --account=AC0123… --sender=Riverside --key-stdin
```

You should see `The site "riverside" now sends text messages with Twilio.` and `Key: ••••` followed by its last 4
characters. The key is stored encrypted and never shown again.

To give every website the same provider instead, put it in `config/tenant.php` (see below) and the key in the
`SMS_API_KEY` environment variable.

chunks.heading: 3. Turn them on and test
chunks.text:
```sh
bin/sightpress site:sms:enable riverside
bin/sightpress site:sms:test riverside --to=+447700900123
```

The test message arrives within a minute: "Test message from Riverside Library: text messages work." If it doesn't,
the command says why in plain words, for example that the key was refused or that the country isn't allowed.

Admins see **Text messages** under **Site settings** in the admin panel: whether the website can send, how much of
this month's budget is used, the latest messages (numbers partly hidden), and **Send a test message**.

chunks.heading: 4. Tell the provider where to report
chunks.text:
In your provider's dashboard, set the delivery reports and incoming messages address to
`https://<your website>/_sms/webhook`. Then a STOP reply stops notifications to that number, and the screen shows
which messages were delivered. Every report must be signed by your provider; others are refused.

chunks.heading: Limits that protect you
chunks.text:
Anyone can type a number into a sign-up form, and some people do that to make websites send expensive texts. So
SightPress:

- only sends to **mobile numbers**, never to premium-rate, shared-cost or toll-free numbers, and checks each new
  number with your provider first;
- only sends to numbers in **your country** (the country of the website's main language), unless you list others;
- sends at most a few codes to one number, one computer and one account each hour, and at most 100 texts a website an
  hour;
- stops at a **monthly budget** (1,000 message parts a website by default), with a warning at 80 %. A small part of
  it is kept for security codes, so people can still sign in when notifications have used the rest.

Change them in `config/tenant.php`:

```php
'sms' => [
    'monthly_budget' => 1000,
    'reserved_for_codes' => 50,
    'countries' => ['GB', 'IE'],
    'limits' => ['per_number' => 3, 'per_client' => 10, 'per_account' => 5, 'per_site' => 100, 'lookups_per_day' => 100],
],
```

chunks.heading: Turn them off
chunks.text:
`bin/sightpress site:sms:disable riverside` stops everything: no texts, no phone sign-in, no codes for important
changes. Numbers already on accounts and the record of messages are kept. `site:sms:remove riverside` also forgets the
website's provider and key.

chunks.heading: Next
chunks.text:
- [Add your mobile number](add-your-mobile-number.md)
- [Get notifications by text](text-message-notifications.md)
- Add a *Text messages* section to your Privacy Policy if your website was made before text messages were on.

On websites with [text messages](set-up-text-messages.md), you can sign in with your confirmed mobile number instead
of your email address. You still need your password.

chunks.heading: Sign in
chunks.text:
1. [Add your mobile number](add-your-mobile-number.md) and confirm it with the code, if you haven't.
2. On the sign-in page, type your number in **Email address or mobile number**, the way you usually write it
   (`07700 900123`) or with `+` and the country code.
3. Type your password and choose **Sign in**.

Only a confirmed number works. After you change your number, the old one stops working at once. If you get "Enter a
correct email address or mobile number, and password.", check both and try again. After 5 wrong tries, wait 15
minutes: tries with your email address and with your number count together.

chunks.heading: Forgot your password?
chunks.text:
1. Choose **Forgot your password?** on the sign-in page.
2. Type your mobile number and choose **Send me a code**. The code comes by text and works for 10 minutes. It never
   contains a link.
3. Type the code, then choose a new password.

We then send an email to your address saying your password was changed after a code to your phone. If it wasn't you,
reset your password with your email address straight away and tell the website's admins.

People who manage the website (users, roles, settings, features or security) can only reset by email, and so can
everyone while the website [asks for a code for important changes](confirm-important-changes.md). That way a stolen or
recycled phone number is not enough to take over an account.

A website can keep its data in a single file on disk (an SQLite database), so it doesn't need a separate database
server. If you want to use one, SightPress can start MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL for you. This guide shows you how.

!!! note "Using it for a website"

    Starting a database server doesn't move any website to it. Choose the database when you
    [create a website](create-a-site.md), with `--db-engine` and the `--db-host`, `--db-name`, `--db-user` and
    `--db-password` options. The server's host name is `mysql`, `mariadb` or `postgres`.

chunks.heading: Start SightPress with a database
chunks.text:
1. If SightPress is running, stop it with `docker compose --profile "*" down`.
2. In the `skeleton` folder, type one of these commands:

    ```sh
    docker compose --profile mysql up
    ```

    For MariaDB, use `--profile mariadb`. For PostgreSQL, use `--profile postgres`.

3. Wait until the text stops scrolling. The first time, Docker downloads the database, which can take a few minutes.
   You should see lines starting with `mysql-1` (or `mariadb-1`, or `postgres-1`) among the others.

To start it in the background instead, add `--detach --wait` to the end of the command.

chunks.heading: Check that the database runs
chunks.text:
1. Open a second terminal and go to the `skeleton` folder.
2. Type:

    ```sh
    docker compose --profile "*" ps
    ```

3. You should see a row for the database, such as `mysql`, with `(healthy)` in the **STATUS** column. If it says
   `(health: starting)`, wait a few seconds and type the command again.

When you start SightPress without `--profile`, no database server runs, and this table has no database row.

chunks.heading: The database settings
chunks.text:
The database is created with these values. You can change them in the `.env` file before the first start (see
[Change the ports SightPress uses](change-the-ports.md#change-a-port) for how to create and edit `.env`).

| Setting            | Default           | What it is                                  |
|--------------------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| `DB_NAME`          | `sightpress`      | The name of the database                    |
| `DB_USER`          | `sightpress`      | The user name                               |
| `DB_PASSWORD`      | `sightpress`      | The user's password                         |
| `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` | `sightpress-root` | The administrator password (MySQL, MariaDB) |

The database server can only be reached by the other SightPress containers, not from your computer or your network.

chunks.heading: Stop the database
chunks.text:
Type `docker compose --profile "*" down`. This stops SightPress and the database. The data in the database is kept
for next time.

If you use a screen reader, a magnifier, a braille display, voice control or switch access, you can tell us how
SightPress works with it before each release. Your experience matters more than any automatic test.

chunks.heading: Before each release
chunks.text:
Before each new version, we post a **Testers wanted** discussion on
[GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/sightpress/core/discussions). It lists the new and changed screens, and how
to try them. Reply there to say you're taking part, or email <contribute@sightpress.org>.

chunks.heading: How to test
chunks.text:
1. Run SightPress on your own computer, as in [Getting started](../getting-started.md), and create a website.
2. Go through the screens listed in the discussion, with the technology you use every day, in the way you normally
   work. For example: sign in, write and publish a page, translate it, search the website, read the analytics.
3. Note anything that stops you, slows you down or surprises you: something not announced, announced twice or
   announced wrongly; focus that jumps or gets lost; a control you can't reach or operate; a chart or table you can't
   understand.
4. Note what worked well too. It tells us what to keep.

We test ourselves with NVDA and Firefox on Windows and VoiceOver and Safari on macOS. Other combinations, such as
JAWS, Narrator, TalkBack, VoiceOver on iOS, Orca, ZoomText or Dragon, are especially welcome.

chunks.heading: Report what you found
chunks.text:
For each problem, [report an accessibility barrier](report-a-problem.md): the task, your assistive technology and its
version, your browser and operating system, what happened and what you expected. Accessibility barriers are always
treated as bugs.

You never need to explain or prove a disability to take part.

Some notifications that a website sends by email can also come by text message, if you choose. The email always comes
too.

| Notification | When you get it |
| --- | --- |
| *When a page is sent to you for review* | Someone sends a page for review and you can publish it. |

chunks.heading: Choose them
chunks.text:
1. [Add your mobile number](add-your-mobile-number.md) if you haven't.
2. On **My account → Mobile number and text messages**, tick **Send me text messages**.
3. Tick the notifications you want, then choose **Save my choices**. You should see "You will get the text messages
   you chose."

chunks.heading: What a text looks like
chunks.text:
> Riverside Library: a page is waiting for your review. Sign in to the admin panel to see it.

Texts are short and in your language. They never contain the page's title or anything else from the page, and never a
link: sign in to the website yourself to see what happened.

Texts are sent within a minute or two. If your organisation's monthly budget for texts is used up, notifications stop
until next month, but emails keep coming.

chunks.heading: Stop them
chunks.text:
Untick **Send me text messages**, remove your number, or reply **STOP** to any of our texts. Reply **START** to get
them again.

chunks.heading: For admins
chunks.text:
**Site settings → Text messages** shows how much of the month's budget is used and the latest messages, with numbers
partly hidden and without their text. **Send a test message** checks that texts arrive.

The admin panel, the website screens (sign-in, search, error pages) and the emails can be translated. Each language
is one file. You need to be fluent in the language; you don't need to be a developer.

chunks.heading: What is translated today
chunks.text:
- **British English** (`en-GB`): the source language, and the language used when a text has no translation.
- **European Portuguese** (`pt-PT`) and **Spanish** (`es`): complete and reviewed.

Regional variants are separate languages: for example Brazilian Portuguese (`pt-BR`) is not European Portuguese, and
Latin American Spanish (`es-419`) is not Spanish from Spain.

chunks.heading: Translate into a new language, or fix a translation
chunks.text:
1. Download the source file,
   [messages.en-GB.xlf](https://github.com/sightpress/core/blob/main/resources/translations/messages.en-GB.xlf), and an
   existing translation as an example, such as
   [messages.es.xlf](https://github.com/sightpress/core/blob/main/resources/translations/messages.es.xlf).
2. Open it in a translation tool that reads XLIFF 2.0 files, such as Poedit, OmegaT or Virtaal, or in a text
   editor. Each text is a `<source>`; write your translation in the `<target>` next to it.
3. Keep the words in curly brackets, such as `{name}` or `{count}`, exactly as they are: SightPress puts a name or a
   number there. Keep any HTML such as `<strong>` too.
4. Use the words people use every day, as the English does. Short sentences are better than long ones.
5. Send the file:
    - by email to <contribute@sightpress.org>, saying which language it is; or
    - as a pull request to the [core repository](https://github.com/sightpress/core), if you know GitHub. The file
      goes in `resources/translations/messages.<code>.xlf`, for example `messages.fr.xlf`.

chunks.heading: What happens next
chunks.text:
- A second fluent speaker reviews every new language, and every new text, before it is released.
- Right-to-left languages, such as Arabic and Hebrew, also get a visual check of every screen.
- New texts that still need a review are marked `state="initial"` in the file. Reviewing them is a good first task.

Translating the documentation is not possible yet: it is written in British English only.
SightPress has a command line tool for tasks such as creating a website. This guide shows you how to run it.

chunks.heading: List the commands
chunks.text:
1. Open a terminal and go to the `skeleton` folder.
2. Type:

    ```sh
    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress list
    ```

3. You should see a list of commands, each with one line about what it does, such as
   `site:create   Creates a site: its database, its first admin and its roles.`

chunks.heading: List your websites
chunks.text:
1. Type:

    ```sh
    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:list
    ```

2. You should see one sentence for each website, with its status, its addresses, its language and its database. If
   you haven't created a website yet, it says "There are no sites yet. Create one with site:create."

chunks.heading: Get help with one command
chunks.text:
1. Type `help` and the name of the command, for example:

    ```sh
    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress help site:create
    ```

2. You should see what the command needs and what each option means.

To create a website, see [Create a website](create-a-site.md). The [command line reference](../reference/command-line.md)
lists every command.

!!! tip "Shortcut for macOS and Linux"

    If the `make` program is installed, `make site-create NAME=demo` runs `site:create demo` and asks for the rest.

Some parts of SightPress are optional **features**, for example site search or visitor statistics. Each website has
its own: an admin can turn a feature off for one website and keep it on for the others. Turning a feature off hides
everything it adds, on the website and in the admin panel, and **keeps its data**, so turning it on again brings it
back as it was.

You need to be an **admin** of the website. Editors, contributors and members don't see the *Features* screen.

!!! note "Optional features in this version"

    This version of SightPress has three optional features of its own: **Site search** (see
    [Search your website](search-your-website.md)), **Analytics** (see
    [See who visits your website](see-who-visits-your-website.md)), both on for new websites, and the
    **AI assistant** (see [Use the AI assistant](use-the-ai-assistant.md)), off for new websites. Features installed
    as extra packages (modules) show up on the screen too: see [Add a module](add-a-module.md).

chunks.heading: See the features of a website
chunks.text:
1. Sign in to the admin panel of the website, for example `http://localhost:8080/admin`.
2. In the admin menu, choose **Features**.
3. You should see one section for each optional feature, with its name as a heading, what it does, its **Status**
   ("On" or "Off") and what happens when it is off.

A feature that says **"set by your organisation"** was chosen for every website by whoever runs your SightPress
installation. It has no button, and it can't be changed from the website.

chunks.heading: Turn a feature off
chunks.text:
1. On the *Features* screen, find the feature and choose **Turn off** followed by its name, for example
   **Turn off Events**.
2. A page asks you to confirm and says what will happen. Choose **Turn off …** again to go ahead, or
   **Keep … on** to go back without changing anything.
3. You are back on the *Features* screen, at the feature's heading. A message at the top says that it is off and that
   its data is kept. Screen readers read the message out.
4. Check: the pages the feature added now answer "not found", and its screens have left the admin menu.

If another feature needs this one, SightPress refuses and names that feature: turn that one off first.

chunks.heading: Turn a feature on
chunks.text:
1. On the *Features* screen, choose **Turn on** followed by the feature's name.
2. You are back at the feature's heading, with the message "… is on."
3. Check: its pages and screens are back, with the data they had before.

If the feature needs another feature that is off, SightPress refuses and names the feature to turn on first.

chunks.heading: Delete a feature's data
chunks.text:
This removes everything the feature stored for the website, **for good**. You can only do it while the feature is off.

1. Turn the feature off (see above).
2. Under the feature, choose **Delete the data of …**. The link only appears when there is data to delete.
3. A page asks you to confirm. Choose **Delete the data of …** to go ahead, or **Keep the data** to go back.
4. The message says the data was deleted. Turning the feature on again later starts afresh, with no data.

Every change on this screen is written to the website's **Audit log**, with who made it and when.

chunks.heading: With the command line tool
chunks.text:
The same can be done in a terminal, in the `skeleton` folder. Replace `demo` with the short name of your website and
`acme.events` with the feature's id, which the first command shows.

1. List the features of a website and whether each one is on:

    ```sh
    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:module:list demo
    ```

2. Turn one on, or off:

    ```sh
    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:module:enable demo acme.events
    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:module:disable demo acme.events
    ```

3. Turn one off and delete its data for good:

    ```sh
    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:module:disable demo acme.events --purge-data
    ```

When you create a website, `site:create demo --without=acme.events` starts it with that feature off.

chunks.heading: For whoever runs the installation
chunks.text:
In `config/tenant.php`, the `modules` section changes the features of **every** website:

- `defaults` says which features new websites start with, for example `'defaults' => ['analytics' => false]`.
  Websites that already exist keep what they have.
- `locked` turns a feature on or off for every website, for example `'locked' => ['analytics' => false]`. Admins then
  see "set by your organisation" and can't change it, and neither can the command line tool.

This guide shows you how to move an installation to a newer version of SightPress, keeping every website, page,
account, menu and setting. It covers updates up to **0.5**.

!!! warning "Make a copy first"

    Before you update, make a copy of the `skeleton` folder, including the `sites` folder and the `.env` file, and of
    every website's database if it isn't an SQLite file in `sites`. Without the `APP_SECRET` from `.env`, SightPress
    can't open the websites' databases.

chunks.heading: Update
chunks.text:
Type these commands in the `skeleton` folder.

1. Stop SightPress: press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> in the window where it runs, or type `docker compose down`.
2. Get the new skeleton:

    ```sh
    git pull
    ```

    If Git says that your changes to `config/tenant.php` or another file would be overwritten, see
    [New settings in 0.3](#new-settings-in-03) and copy the new parts in by hand.

3. Get the new version of SightPress itself:

    ```sh
    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php composer update
    ```

4. Update the list of websites to the new format (from 0.4 on, it can hold each website's upload limits):

    ```sh
    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:registry:upgrade
    ```

    You should see that the file was upgraded, or that there is nothing to do. The old file is kept as
    `config/sites.php.bak`.

5. Update the database tables of every website:

    ```sh
    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:migrate --all
    ```

    You should see one line per website saying how many database migrations ran. One website failing doesn't stop
    the others; run it again for that website once the problem is fixed.

6. Build the search index of each website, replacing `demo` with its short name:

    ```sh
    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:search:reindex demo
    ```

7. Start SightPress again with `docker compose up`. The **scheduler** starts with it now (see below).
8. Check: sign in to

chunks.heading: What changes for your websites
chunks.text:
- **Site search** and **Analytics** are **on** for every website after the update. Turn them off on the
  [Features](turn-features-on-or-off.md) screen if you don't want them.
- The **AI assistant** is **off**. Nothing is sent to any AI service until an admin sets it up; see
  [Use the AI assistant](use-the-ai-assistant.md).
- **Sign-up** is off and every website is still readable by everyone, as before.
- The *Privacy notice* starter page of websites made before the update doesn't describe analytics. Add a section
  about it yourself; [See who visits your website](see-who-visits-your-website.md) explains what is counted.

chunks.heading: New settings in 0.3
chunks.text:
- `.env` has a block of **upload limits** (`UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE`, `INPUT_MAX_SIZE` and others). Copy the block from
  `.env.example`; without it, the recommended values are used. See [Fix upload size limits](fix-upload-size-limits.md).
- `config/tenant.php` has two new sections: `modules`, which sets the features of every website (see
  [Turn features on or off](turn-features-on-or-off.md#for-whoever-runs-the-installation)), and `uploads`, which
  tells SightPress the web server's limit.
- `docker-compose.yml` has a **scheduler** service, which publishes scheduled pages and keeps the analytics up to
  date. It runs `bin/sightpress schedule:run` once a minute. On a server without Docker, add this line to the
  crontab of the user that runs SightPress (`crontab -e`), with the path of your project:

    ```text
    * * * * * cd /var/www/my-site && php bin/sightpress schedule:run --no-interaction >> var/log/schedule.log 2>&1
    ```

    Run it in one place only per installation.

chunks.heading: New in 0.4
chunks.text:
Follow the same steps. Step 4 is needed for this update. After it:

- **The look of your websites stays the same.** The default theme now comes as its own package, which Composer
  installs. `composer update` also publishes the theme files and previews.
- **Your files stay where they are.** Nothing moves to the cloud unless you [set it up](keep-files-in-the-cloud.md).
- A **published page with a video without captions, or a recording without a transcript, stays published**, but the
  publish check asks for them the next time it is published. See
  [Add captions and transcripts](add-captions-and-transcripts.md).

`config/tenant.php` has new optional sections. Copy them from the new skeleton if Git can't merge them:

- `themes`: which installed themes websites may use, and the theme of new websites.
- `media.limits`: every website's upload limits and the most a website may set.
- `uploads.temp_path` and `uploads.max_chunked_bytes`: where large files wait while their parts arrive, and the largest
  file that can be sent in parts.

chunks.heading: New in 0.5
chunks.text:
Follow the same steps, including updating the websites' databases (`site:migrate --all`). After it:

- **Nothing changes for your websites until you choose to.** Text messages are off, so nobody is asked for a mobile
  number and the sign-in page still says "Email address". Two-step confirmation is off. No email or domain policy
  applies. Custom roles, text messages and two-step confirmation are there to set up when you want them: see
  [Create a custom role](create-a-custom-role.md), [Set up text messages](set-up-text-messages.md) and
  [Confirm important changes](confirm-important-changes.md).
- **Modules you install from now on start off** on the websites that already exist; an admin turns them on. See
  [Add a module](add-a-module.md).

`config/tenant.php` has new optional settings. Copy them from the new skeleton if Git can't merge them, or leave them
out to keep the defaults. Each one is described in the [tenant configuration reference](../reference/tenant-config.md):

- `domain_policy`, `email_policy` and `domain_registration`: keep websites and accounts to your organisation's domains
  (see [Keep websites to your organisation](keep-websites-to-your-organisation.md));
- `sms`: a text message provider every website may use, the monthly budget and the limits;
- `two_step`: whether websites may, must or must not ask for a code before important changes.

`.env.example` names `SMS_API_KEY` and `ASSISTANT_API_KEY`, for the keys of providers you set in `config/tenant.php`.

chunks.heading: For module authors
chunks.text:
Modules need `sightpress/module-interface` `^0.5`. The events a module listens to moved from core into the contract,
under `SightPress\Module\Event` (for example `SightPress\Module\Event\PageTransitioned`), and values that were enums
are strings there. Change the `use` lines of your subscribers and remove any dependency on `sightpress/core` outside
`require-dev`. The [module interface reference](../reference/module-interface.md) lists every event with its fields.

chunks.heading: If something goes wrong
chunks.text:
**A website shows an error page after the update**
:   Its database tables are older than the code. Run `site:migrate` for it (step 5) and read the message it prints.

**An error says `config/sites.php` uses an older format version**
:   Run `site:registry:upgrade` (step 4).

**`composer update` fails**
:   Check that you are in the `skeleton` folder and that SightPress is stopped, then try again. Your websites are
    not changed until step 4.

**Search finds nothing**
:   Pages are added to the search index when they are published or changed. Run step 6 for that website to add
    the pages that were already there.

SightPress sends large files in small parts. If your connection drops, or you close the page, you can carry on from
where the upload stopped instead of starting again.

If your website keeps its files in **cloud storage**, large files go straight from your browser to the storage, which
is faster and doesn't load your server. If the storage doesn't allow that, SightPress sends the file through your
server instead and says so. You don't need to do anything different.

chunks.heading: Upload a large file
chunks.text:
1. In the admin, open **Media**.
2. Under **Upload a file**, choose your file. The hint under the field says the largest file of each kind.
3. Choose **Upload**.

A progress bar shows how far the upload has gone. Screen readers hear the progress every 10%. When it finishes,
SightPress checks the file and opens its page, so you can describe it.

chunks.heading: Pause, resume or cancel
chunks.text:
While a large file is uploading, three buttons work by keyboard or mouse:

- **Pause** stops sending. Focus moves to **Resume**.
- **Resume** carries on from where it stopped.
- **Cancel upload** stops and deletes what was sent so far.

chunks.heading: If the upload stops
chunks.text:
- **The connection dropped.** SightPress tries again by itself. If it still can't connect, it pauses and asks you to
  choose **Resume**.
- **You closed or reloaded the page.** Open **Media**, choose **the same file** and choose **Upload**. It carries on
  from where it stopped, on the same computer and browser, for up to 24 hours.

chunks.heading: If the file is refused
chunks.text:
SightPress checks what a file really is once it has arrived, whatever its name says. A file of a type it doesn't
accept is deleted, and **Media** explains why.

chunks.heading: For whoever runs the server
chunks.text:
- To see which way large files travel, and why, open **Site settings**, then **File storage**. For files to go straight
  to cloud storage, its CORS rules must allow `PUT` from your website's address and expose `ETag`. `site:storage:provision`
  sets this up on AWS and Cloudflare.
- Files that go through the server wait in `var/uploads`. To use another folder, set `uploads.temp_path` in `config/tenant.php`. It
  can't be inside `public`.
- The largest file that can be sent in parts is 5 GB. To change it, set `uploads.max_chunked_bytes`. Each website's own
  limits still apply, see [Choose upload limits](choose-upload-limits.md).
- If your website runs on **several servers**, they must share the upload folder. Otherwise people see a message saying
  the server doesn't have the file's earlier parts.
- Abandoned uploads are removed after 24 hours by the [scheduler](run-in-the-background.md). To see the uploads in
  progress, or remove abandoned ones now:

    ```sh
    docker compose exec php bin/sightpress site:media:uploads demo
    docker compose exec php bin/sightpress site:media:uploads demo --purge-expired
    ```

Without JavaScript, a file is sent in one piece, so the lower server limit applies. See
[Fix upload size limits](fix-upload-size-limits.md).

The AI assistant suggests text for your website: summaries, descriptions for search engines, alt text for pictures,
drafts of pages and translations. It also answers questions about using SightPress. It uses an AI service you
choose, with **your own key** from that service, so you pay the service directly for what you use.

The assistant only ever **suggests**. Nothing it writes is used until a person inserts it and saves. Alt text and
translations it writes are marked until a person has checked them, and pages that use them can't be published
before that.

The AI assistant is an optional feature, **off** for new websites. Nothing is sent to any AI service until an admin
sets it up and someone asks for a suggestion.

chunks.heading: Before you start
chunks.text:
- You need to be an **admin** of the website to turn the assistant on and set it up.
- You need an **API key** from one of the AI services SightPress works with: Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT),
  Mistral AI, or a service or your own server that works like OpenAI's. Each service's website explains how to get
  a key and what it costs. Check where the service processes data before you choose it: Mistral AI, for example,
  processes it in the EU.

chunks.heading: Turn the assistant on
chunks.text:
1. Sign in to the admin panel, for example at `http://localhost:8080/admin`.
2. In the admin menu, choose **Features**.
3. Find **AI assistant** and choose **Turn on AI assistant**.
4. You should see that its status is now "On". A new screen appears in the admin menu under **Site settings**:
   **AI assistant**.

See [Turn features on or off](turn-features-on-or-off.md) for more about features.

chunks.heading: Choose the service and enter your key
chunks.text:
1. In the admin menu, choose **Site settings**, then **AI assistant**.
2. Under **Status** you should see "Not ready yet", followed by what is missing.
3. Under **AI service**, choose a service. Each one says what it is.
4. Choose a **Model**. Bigger models write better and cost more. For an OpenAI-compatible service, type the
   **Model name** and the **Address of the service** instead (it must start with `https://`).
5. Paste your key into **New API key** and choose **Save the AI service**.
6. You should see "The AI service is saved." Under **Status** it now says "Ready", and the page shows only the last
   four characters of your key, for example "Saved API key: ••••1234". The key is stored encrypted and never shown
   again. To change it, paste a new one; to delete it, choose **Remove key**.
7. Choose **Test connection**. You should see "The connection works", or what went wrong (for example a key the
   service didn't accept).

If your organisation chooses the AI service for every website, this screen shows its choice and you can't change
it.

chunks.heading: Choose who may use it, and a budget
chunks.text:
1. On the same screen, under **Who may use it, and how much**, tick the roles that may ask the assistant. Admins
   always may.
2. In **Monthly budget in tokens**, enter how many tokens (pieces of words, sent and received) the website may use
   each month. Leave it empty to use your organisation's budget; enter 0 for no limit.
3. Choose **Save who may use it**. The screen shows how much has been used this month.

Months start on the 1st. From 80% of the budget, everyone who asks is warned; at 100% the assistant stops until the
next month. Each person can ask 20 times every 10 minutes.

chunks.heading: Ask a question
chunks.text:
1. On the **Dashboard** (or at the end of a page's editor), find **Ask the assistant**.
2. Type your question in **Your question**, for example "How do I add a page to the main menu?", and choose
   **Ask**.
3. You should hear or see "Working on it…", then "Suggestion ready". The answer appears under its own heading,
   which gets focus. It ends with a link to the part of this documentation it used.

The assistant only tells you about screens your role can use. If something needs an admin, it says so.

On a page's editor you can tick **Share this page with the assistant** to ask about the page itself. It reads the
saved page, so save your changes first.

chunks.heading: Get a suggestion for a field
chunks.text:
On a page's editor, under **Summary**, **Title in search results** and **Description for search engines**, there is a
**Suggest** button.

1. Save the page first: the assistant reads the saved page.
2. Choose, for example, **Suggest a summary**.
3. The suggestion appears in **Ask the assistant**, under its own heading, which gets focus.
