4. Choose **Insert** to put it in the field (focus goes back to the field), **Copy** to copy it, **Try again** for
   another one, or **Discard**.
5. Check the text, change it if needed, and choose **Save page**.

Without JavaScript, the same buttons open a page with the suggestion; **Insert** takes you back to the field with
the text in it.

chunks.heading: Rewrite text, draft a page, or explain a check
chunks.text:
- **Rewrite text** (in every **Ask the assistant**): paste some text, choose **Make it** simpler, shorter, friendlier
  or more formal, and choose **Rewrite**. Copy the result into your page.
- **Draft this page** (on a page's editor): say what the page should be about and choose **Draft this page**.
  Choose **Add to the end of the page**: the headings and text are added to the page's blocks, not yet saved.
  Things to check or fill in are in [square brackets].
- **Explain this** (next to each publish check on a page's editor): the assistant explains what the check means
  and how to fix it.

chunks.heading: Alt text for pictures
chunks.text:
The assistant can describe pictures only with a model that can see pictures (most listed models can).

1. In the admin menu, choose **Media** and open a picture.
2. Under the alt text field, choose **Suggest alt text**.
3. Choose **Insert**, check the text, and choose **Save details**.
4. You should see "The AI assistant suggested this alt text." Pages that show this text can't be published until
   someone checks it.
5. When the text describes the picture well, tick **I checked the alt text: it describes the picture** and choose
   **Save details**. Changing the text and saving it counts as checking it too.

chunks.heading: Draft a translation
chunks.text:
On a website in more than one language:

1. Open a page's editor. In the **Translations** section, choose **Draft a translation into** followed by the
   language, **with the AI assistant**.
2. The new translation opens in the editor, with a notice: "The AI assistant drafted this translation, and nobody
   has checked it yet." Its blocks, pictures and links are the same as the original's; only the words are
   translated.
3. Read it and change what needs changing. Then save the page, or choose **I checked this translation**.
4. Only then can the translation be published. Until then the list of pages and the page's older versions say
   "drafted by the AI assistant, not checked yet".

chunks.heading: What is sent, and what is kept
chunks.text:
- Sent to the AI service: your question, and the page or picture you ask a suggestion for. Never lists of people,
  email addresses, the audit log or other pages.
- Kept on your website: when the assistant was used, by whom, for what, with which service and model, and how many
  tokens. Never the question, the page text or the answer.
- The AI service handles what it receives under its own terms.

chunks.heading: Turn the assistant off
chunks.text:
On the **Features** screen, choose **Turn off AI assistant**. The panel, the Suggest buttons and the AI assistant
screen disappear. The settings, the key and the record of what was used are kept, so turning it on again brings
everything back.

chunks.heading: From the command line
chunks.text:
Whoever runs your SightPress installation can set the assistant up with `site:assistant:set`, test it with
`site:assistant:test`, see what was used with `site:assistant:usage` and turn it off with
`site:assistant:disable`. See the [command line reference](../reference/command-line.md#ai-assistant).

This guide shows you how to start a page, add its content, and take it through review until visitors can read it.
Every step works with a keyboard alone and with a screen reader.

You need an account on the website with the role contributor, editor or admin. See
[Roles and permissions](../reference/roles-and-permissions.md).

chunks.heading: Start a page
chunks.text:
1. Sign in to the website, for example at <http://localhost:8080/login>. You should see the **Dashboard**.
2. Choose **Pages** in the admin menu, then **Start a new page**. You should see the heading **Start a new page**.
3. In **Title**, type the page's title, for example `Book club`. You can change it later.
4. In **Put it under**, choose where the page belongs. Choose **None: a top-level page** for a page of its own, or
   another page to put it under that one. A page under "About us" gets an address such as `/about/book-club`.
5. Leave **Layout** on **Standard page**. **Home page** shows the title and summary as a large introduction.
6. Choose **Start the page**. You should see the message "“Book club” has been started as a draft. Add its content,
   then save it." and the heading **Edit “Book club”**.

A new page is a **draft**: nobody else sees it until it is published.

chunks.heading: Add the content
chunks.text:
A page is made of **blocks**, shown one after another: a heading, some text, a picture and so on. The [blocks reference](../reference/blocks.md) describes every kind. 1. Go to the **Content** section. On a new page it says "There are no blocks yet. Add the first one below." 2. In **Type of block to add**, choose a kind of block, for example **Text**. 3. Choose **Add block**. You should hear or see "Added a Text block. It is block 1 of 1. Save the page to keep this change." Focus moves to the new block, a group called "Block 1 of 1: Text". 4. Fill in the block's fields. For a Text block, type your text in **Text**. You can use simple HTML, such as `

We meet every first Tuesday of the month.

`. **Update the previews** shows how it will look. 5. Add more blocks the same way. Each block has the buttons **Move up**, **Move down** and **Remove**. After each one, you hear or see what changed, for example "Moved block 2 (Text) up. It is now block 1 of 2." Focus stays on the block or on the button. 6. Choose **Save page**. It is at the top and at the bottom of the form; pressing Enter in a field saves too. You should see "Saved “Book club”." !!! warning "The block buttons don't save" Adding, moving and removing blocks changes the form only. Nothing is kept until you choose **Save page**. If the page can't be saved, a list of problems appears at the top of the page and gets focus. Each problem is a link to the field it is about

chunks.heading: Help people find the page
chunks.text:
The **Search & AI** section decides how the page looks in search engines, in AI search and when it is shared. All
its fields are optional, but a description and a summary help people find the page.

- **Summary**: one or two sentences about the page. Shown in lists of pages and read by AI search engines.
- **Title in search results**: only when it should differ from the page title.
- **Description for search engines**: one or two sentences. Search engines show about 160 characters. A count of
  the characters is read out after a short pause.
- **Ask search engines and AI search engines not to list this page**: tick it to keep the page out of search
  results. It is then also left out of the sitemap and `llms.txt`.

**How a search result could look** shows the title, the address and the description as text. Choose **Update the
previews** after a change. [Search and AI visibility](../reference/search-and-ai.md) explains the rest.

chunks.heading: Check the page before you send it
chunks.text:
Under the form, SightPress checks the saved page:

- **Problems that stop publishing**, for example a picture without alt text, a video without captions or a heading
  that skips a level. A page with these can't be published until they are fixed.
- **Suggestions**, for example "Add a description for search engines". The page can be published with these.

Each item links to the field or block it is about. When there are only suggestions, the check says "Ready to
publish, with suggestions".

chunks.heading: Send the page for review
chunks.text:
Contributors, editors and admins all send their pages for review.

1. Save the page first. The review buttons use the saved page.
2. Under **Review and publishing**, you can write a **Note for the next person**, for example what you changed.
3. Choose **Submit for review**. You should see "Sent for review. The editors have been told by email."

The page now waits for review. Every editor and admin gets an e-mail with the page's name and a link to it in the
admin panel. A contributor can't change the page while it waits.

chunks.heading: Review, approve and publish a page
chunks.text:
You need the role editor or admin.

1. Open the page: choose the link in the e-mail, or find the page under **Waiting for review** on the **Dashboard**.
2. Read the page. **View the saved page**, at the top, shows it as visitors will see it.
3. If it needs changes, choose **Send back to draft**, with a note that says what to change. You should see "Sent
   back to draft. The writer can change it and send it again."
4. If it is ready, choose **Approve**. You should see "Approved. It can be published now."
5. Choose **Publish**. You should see "Published. Visitors can see the page now."

If the page still has a problem that stops publishing, **Publish** is refused, and the list of problems appears at
the top with focus on it.

chunks.heading: Look at the published page
chunks.text:
1. Go to the page's address on the website, for example <http://localhost:8080/book-club>. The address is shown
   next to **State** at the top of the page editor.
2. You should see the page with its content. It is now also in the website's sitemap and its `llms.txt` file.

chunks.heading: Take a page off the website
chunks.text:
1. Open the page in the admin panel.
2. Choose **Unpublish**. You should see "Unpublished. Visitors can’t see the page any more; it is a draft again."

The page becomes a draft and goes through review again before it is back on the website.

SightPress is a powerful content management system (CMS) for everyone, designed with blind and low-vision
creators and audiences in mind. It is built on modern, object-oriented PHP and is free software, licensed
under the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later.

With SightPress you can run many websites from one installation, each in as many languages as you need.
The admin area, the default theme and every built-in feature aim to meet the Web Content Accessibility
Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA. Every task works with a keyboard alone and with a screen reader.

chunks.heading: Status
chunks.text:
This is the first version of SightPress (0.1). You can create websites from the command line, and each website has
ready-made pages, an admin panel to write and publish pages through review, a media library, menus, invitations,
site settings and an audit log. Every page is ready for search engines and AI readers.

chunks.heading: Where to go next
chunks.text:
- To see what SightPress can do, with ideas for websites, read [What you can build](what-you-can-build.md).
- The source code lives on GitHub in the [SightPress organisation](https://github.com/sightpress).
- To run SightPress on your own computer, follow [Getting started](getting-started.md).
- To make a theme of your own, follow the tutorial [Create a theme](tutorials/create-a-theme.md).
- To make a module of your own, follow the tutorial [Create a module](tutorials/create-a-module.md).
- The [how-to guides](how-to/index.md) show you how to do one task at a time, such as
  [creating a website](how-to/create-a-site.md) or [writing and publishing a page](how-to/write-and-publish-a-page.md).
- The reference pages explain [roles and permissions](reference/roles-and-permissions.md), [blocks](reference/blocks.md),
  [search and AI visibility](reference/search-and-ai.md) and the [command line tool](reference/command-line.md).

A page's content is a list of **blocks**, shown one after another. Each kind of block holds one kind of content, such
as a heading, some text or a picture. SightPress comes with thirteen kinds. Add-on modules can add more.

This page lists every kind, its fields and their limits, and what SightPress checks for accessibility. To add, move
and remove blocks, see [Write and publish a page](../how-to/write-and-publish-a-page.md).

chunks.heading: How blocks are checked
chunks.text:
- **When you save**, every block is checked. Every problem is listed at once, at the top of the page, with a link to
  the field, for example "Heading text: Fill in this field." Nothing is saved until every block is fine.
- **When you publish**, SightPress checks the page for accessibility. Problems marked "stops publishing" below must be
  fixed first. Problems marked "suggestion" don't stop publishing.
- **Files** come from the website's media library and must be the right kind, for example a picture for an Image
  block. Visitors only see files that are published in the media library; a page that uses an unpublished file
  can't be published.
- **Every block also has a text version**, which AI search engines and other readers get as Markdown. See
  [Search and AI visibility](search-and-ai.md).

Fields marked *required* must be filled in. All the others are optional.

chunks.heading: Heading
chunks.text:
A heading that starts a part of the page.

| Field | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| **Heading text** (required) | Up to 200 characters. |
| **Level** (required) | 2 to 6. Level 2 starts a main part of the page, 3 a part of that, and so on. The page title is the only level 1. |

- Stops publishing: a heading that skips a level, such as a level 4 straight after a level 2.

chunks.heading: Text
chunks.text:
Formatted text: paragraphs, lists, links and more. | Field | Limits | | --- | --- | | **Text** (required) | Up to 100,000 characters, written as HTML. | You can use paragraphs `

`, headings `

` to `

`, lists `
    `, `
      ` and `
    1. `, links ``, `` and ``. Quotes, code, abbreviations and description lists work too, and a text or background colour written as `style="color: #1a1a1a"` or `style="background-color: #ffeb3b"`. Anything else is removed when you save. Scripts, embedded frames and pictures are always removed; use an Image block for pictures. Text pasted from other editors keeps its words. - Stops publishing: a link with no text; a level 1 heading or a heading that skips a level; a colour that is too faint to read (a contrast below 4.5 to 1, in light or dark mode); a language code that isn't real. - Suggestion: link text that doesn't say where it goes, such as "click here", "read more" or a bare web address.

chunks.heading: Image
chunks.text:
One picture from the media library.

| Field | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| **Image** (required) | A picture from the media library. |
| **Alternative text** | Up to 1,000 characters. What the picture shows, for people who can't see it. |
| **The picture is only decoration: screen readers skip it** | Tick it only for a picture that adds nothing to the page. |
| **Caption** | Up to 2,000 characters. Shown under the picture, for everyone. |

- Stops publishing: no alternative text, when the picture isn't marked as decoration.
- Suggestion: alternative text that looks like a file name, starts with "image of", or is longer than 250 characters.

chunks.heading: Gallery
chunks.text:
A set of pictures, shown as a list so that screen readers say how many there are.

| Field | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| **Pictures** (required) | 1 to 50 pictures. Each has **Picture**, **Alternative text**, the decoration tick box and **Caption**, as in an Image block. |
| **Caption of the gallery** | Up to 2,000 characters. Shown under all the pictures. |

Every picture is checked like an Image block.

chunks.heading: Video
chunks.text:
A video from the media library, with captions and a transcript. It never starts by itself.

| Field | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| **Video** (required) | A video from the media library. |
| **Title** (required) | Up to 200 characters. Names the video for screen readers and search engines. |
| **Captions** | A WebVTT captions file (`.vtt`) from the media library. |
| **Language of the captions** | A language tag such as `en-GB`. Leave it empty for the page's language. |
| **The video has no speech or important sounds, so it needs no captions** | A tick box. |
| **Poster picture** | A picture shown before the video plays. |
| **Transcript** | Up to 100,000 characters. Everything said and shown, as text. Shown under the video behind a **Transcript** button. |

- Stops publishing: a video with speech but no captions; a video marked as having no speech, but with no transcript
  that describes what it shows.
- Suggestion: a video without a transcript.

A captions file is a plain text file whose first line is `WEBVTT`. Upload it to the media library like any other
file.

chunks.heading: Audio
chunks.text:
A sound recording from the media library, with a transcript. It never starts by itself.

| Field | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| **Audio** (required) | A sound file from the media library. |
| **Title** (required) | Up to 200 characters. Names the recording for screen readers and search engines. |
| **Transcript** | Up to 100,000 characters. Everything said, as text. Shown under the player behind a **Transcript** button. |

- Stops publishing: no transcript.

chunks.heading: File download
chunks.text:
A link to a file from the media library, such as a PDF.

| Field | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| **File** (required) | A file from the media library. |
| **Link text** (required) | Up to 200 characters. What the file is, for example "Annual report 2026". |

SightPress adds the file's type and size to the link, written for the page's language: "Annual report 2026 (PDF,
2.3 MB)".

- Suggestion: link text that says nothing on its own, such as "here" or "details".

chunks.heading: Call to action
chunks.text:
A button that leads somewhere.

| Field | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| **Button text** (required) | Up to 80 characters. Say what happens, for example "Book a visit". |
| **Link address** (required) | Up to 2,000 characters. A page of this website, such as `/contact`, a full address such as `https://example.org`, or a `mailto:` or `tel:` address. |
| **Style** | Primary for the main action of the page, secondary for others. |

- Suggestion: button text that doesn't say what happens, such as "click here".

chunks.heading: Columns
chunks.text:
Two to four columns side by side on wide screens, one after another on narrow screens and when zoomed in. The
columns are read in order: the first column, then the second.

| Field | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| **Columns** (required) | 2 to 4 columns. |
| **Blocks** in each column | Up to 50 blocks of any kind except Columns. |

Every block in a column is checked as if it were on the page.

chunks.heading: Contact form
chunks.text:
A form visitors use to send you a message. It has fields for their name, e-mail address and message.

| Field | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| **Send messages to** (required) | The e-mail address that gets the messages. It is never shown on the page. |
| **Email subject** | Up to 100 characters. The subject of the e-mails you get. |
| **Button text** | Up to 40 characters. |
| **Message after sending** | Up to 300 characters. The thank-you message visitors see. |

- Messages arrive from the website's own address. Reply to them as usual: the reply goes to the visitor.
- Spam is kept out without a puzzle: a hidden field that people never see, and at most 5 messages per visitor every
  10 minutes.
- When something is missing, the visitor comes back to the same page with a list of what to fix, which gets focus,
  and what they typed is kept. After sending, the thank-you message gets focus.
- The form only works on a published, public page.

chunks.heading: Video or map from another site
chunks.text:
A YouTube or Vimeo video, or an OpenStreetMap map, shown from its link.

| Field | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| **Link to the video or map** (required) | Up to 2,000 characters. Only YouTube, Vimeo and OpenStreetMap links are accepted. |
| **Title** (required) | Up to 200 characters. Says what it shows, for example "Map of the library". |

- Nothing loads from the other site until the reader presses **Show the video** or **Show the map**. Until then the
  block says who the provider is and links to their privacy policy and to the original. Without JavaScript, the link
  is there.
- YouTube videos use YouTube's privacy-enhanced address, and Vimeo is asked not to track.

chunks.heading: List of pages
chunks.text:
A list of pages that keeps itself up to date.

| Field | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| **Which pages** (required) | The pages under a page, or the pages changed most recently. |
| **Under the page at** | The address of a page of this website, such as `/services`. Leave it empty for the top-level pages. |
| **How many pages, at most** | 1 to 12. |
| **Show each page's summary** | A tick box. |

- Shown as a list or as cards (choose under the block's look). Each page has one link.
- It only lists pages everyone may read: members-only pages never appear, not even in the Markdown version, `llms.txt`
  or search results. On a members-only website the list stays empty for now.
- The home page and the page the list is on are never in the list.

chunks.heading: Sign language video
chunks.text:
A video in a sign language, such as British Sign Language (BSL), Irish Sign Language or International Sign.

| Field | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| **Video** (required) | A video from the media library. |
| **Title** (required) | Up to 200 characters, for example "This page in British Sign Language". |
| **Sign language** (required) | The sign language the video is in. It is shown under the video. |
| **Captions** (required) | A WebVTT captions file (`.vtt`), for people who don't sign or use another sign language. |
| **Language of the captions** | A language tag such as `en-GB`. Leave it empty for the page's language. |
| **Poster picture** | A picture shown before the video plays. |
| **Transcript** | What is signed, as text. |

chunks.heading: The look of a block
chunks.text:
Under **Look of block n**, each block can have its own look. A choice changes only that block.

| Choice | Values | Offered on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Style** | Named looks, for example *Rounded corners* for a picture or *Card* for a form. Modules can add more. | Image, Contact form, List of pages, and module blocks |
| **Text alignment** | Start (default), Centre, End. Start and End flip in right-to-left languages. | Heading, Text, Call to action |
| **Background** | None (default), Surface, Muted, Accent, in the theme's colours. | Text, Columns, Contact form |
| **Width** | Text width (default), Wide, Full width. | Text, Image, Columns, Gallery, Video |
| **Space above and below** | Medium (default), None, Small, Large. | Every block |
| **Form layout**, **Form size**, **Button position** | Labels above or beside the fields; small, medium or large; button at the start, the end or full width. | Contact form |

- Text always has enough contrast: backgrounds come from the theme, and SightPress checks every theme's colours.
- Labels beside the fields go back above them when there isn't room, such as on a phone or when zoomed in.
- Centred text gets a hint, because it is harder to read over more than a few lines.

chunks.heading: For developers
chunks.text:
A module adds a kind of block with `$registrar->blockTypes()->add(MyBlock::class)`, a class that implements
`SightPress\Module\Block\BlockType`. Names of other modules' kinds need a vendor prefix, such as `acme.event_card`.

The fields come from the block's JSON Schema (draft 2020-12). Give every field a `title` (its label) and a
`description` (its hint). Core enforces only these keywords, and refuses a schema with any other, so no rule is ever
skipped without notice: `type`, `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties`, `enum`, `minLength`, `maxLength`,
`pattern`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `items`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `format` and `contentMediaType: text/html` (rich
text, cleaned on save). The formats are `link`, `email`, `media`, `media-image`, `media-video`, `media-audio`,
`media-document` and `media-captions`.

Core's own kinds are named `heading`, `rich_text`, `image`, `gallery`, `video`, `audio`, `file_download`,
`call_to_action`, `columns` and `contact_form`.

SightPress has a command line tool, `bin/sightpress`, for the tasks that are done once per website or by whoever runs
the installation: creating websites, turning them on and off, and moving them. Everyday work, such as writing pages
and inviting people, happens in each website's admin panel.

The tool writes plain sentences, without tables or colours, so that its answers read well with a screen reader. It
never shows a database password.

chunks.heading: How to run it
chunks.text:
With the `skeleton` running in Docker, start every command from the `skeleton` folder with
`docker compose run --rm --no-deps php`, for example:

```sh
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress list
```

You should see every command with one line about what it does. For the details of one command, type
`bin/sightpress help` and its name, for example `bin/sightpress help site:create`.

Most commands need `APP_SECRET` to be set (see step 6 of [Getting started](../getting-started.md)).

chunks.heading: How commands ask questions
site:create
chunks.text:
```text
site:create [<slug>] [--domain=] [--db= | --db-engine= --db-path= | --db-host= --db-port= --db-name= --db-user= --db-password=]
            [--owner-type=] [--locale=] [--admin-email=] [--admin-first-name=] [--admin-last-name=]
            [--name=] [--timezone=] [--url=] [--create-db] [--with-demo-content] [--without=]
            [--domain-registration=tenant|off]
```

Creates a website: its database tables, its roles, its first admin, six starter pages, its menus and its logo, icon
and share image. It prints the first admin's setup code. Nothing is created if something is wrong.
[Create a website](../how-to/create-a-site.md) explains every option. `--without=` names optional features (module
ids, separated by commas) the website starts with off. `--domain-registration=off` turns your organisation's
registration with an organisation email address off for this website. When your installation has a `domain_policy`
or an `email_policy`, the domains and the first admin's address must follow it (see
[Keep websites to your organisation](../how-to/keep-websites-to-your-organisation.md)).

chunks.heading: site:user:create-admin
chunks.text:
```text
site:user:create-admin <slug> --email= --first-name= --last-name= [--url=] [--phone=]
```

Creates an admin on a website and prints the setup code they choose their password with. For an admin who hasn't
chosen a password yet, it prints a new code, and the old one stops working. Someone who can already sign in is
refused: they use "Forgot your password?" instead. `--phone=` gives them a confirmed mobile number (for text
messages and two-step confirmation): you vouch that it is theirs, so no code is sent.

chunks.heading: site:user:phone:reset
chunks.text:
```text
site:user:phone:reset <slug> <email>
```

Removes the mobile number of an account, for example after its owner lost their phone, so they can add a new one. It
works whatever two-step confirmation says. See [Lost your phone](../how-to/lost-your-phone.md).

chunks.heading: Turn websites on and off
chunks.text:
| Command | What it does | Visitors see |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `site:enable <slug>` | Turns a website on, so it answers again. Also brings back a deleted website. | the website |
| `site:disable <slug>` | Turns a website off for a while. | "temporarily unavailable" (503) |
| `site:archive <slug>` | Archives a website. Its data is kept. | "gone" (410) |
| `site:delete <slug>` | Deletes a website, softly: it stops answering and its data is kept until `site:purge`. | "not found" (404) |
| `site:purge <slug> [--drop-database]` | Removes a deleted website for good. Its database is kept unless you add `--drop-database`, which can't be undone. | — |

Every change is written to the installation's log.

chunks.heading: Look after websites
chunks.text:
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `site:list` | Lists the websites: status, domains, language, time zone and database (engine, host and name only). |
| `site:migrate <slug>` or `site:migrate --all` | Updates a website's database tables after an update of SightPress. `--all` updates every website that isn't deleted; one failure doesn't stop the others. |
| `site:db:change <slug> [--db= or the --db-… parts] [--migrate]` | Points a **disabled** website at another database, asked for in parts like in `site:create`. **Nothing is copied**: move the data first. The new database must be up to date, or add `--migrate`. If anything fails, the website keeps its old database. |
| `site:seo:check <slug>` | Checks what search engines will find: titles longer than 60 characters, missing or too long descriptions, pages left out of search and why. Ends with an error when two pages have the same title. See [Search and AI visibility](search-and-ai.md). |

| `system:check [--site=<slug>] [--probe-url=<address>] [--recommend]` | Lists the server's upload and input limits, the largest file of each kind that can be uploaded, and the settings to change. Ends with an error when something must be fixed. `--site` checks one website's limits and counts the uploads refused for it. `--probe-url` sends test requests to find the web server's real limit. `--recommend` prints the server values the limits need. It also notes websites and accounts outside a `domain_policy` or `email_policy` that was ma

chunks.heading: Languages
chunks.text:
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `site:locale:add <slug> <locale>` | Adds a language to the website, for example `site:locale:add demo pt-PT`. Pages are then translated into it from each page's editor. |
| `site:locale:default <slug> <locale>` | Makes one of the website's languages the main one, whose pages have addresses without a language part. Warns that addresses change. |
| `site:locale:remove <slug> <locale> [--yes]` | Removes a language. Without `--yes` it only explains what would happen. Its translations are kept, unreachable, and come back if the language is added again. The main language can't be removed. |

See [Add a language and translate a page](../how-to/add-a-language.md).

chunks.heading: schedule:run
chunks.text:
```text
schedule:run
```

Does everything that is due on every website that is on: publishes and unpublishes scheduled pages, rolls up and
deletes old analytics, rebuilds search indexes that are out of date and removes sign-ups that were never confirmed.
It prints a line for each thing it did and a summary. Run it **once a minute**: the skeleton's `scheduler` service does
this in Docker; on a server, add a crontab line (see [Update SightPress](../how-to/update-sightpress.md#new-settings-in-03)).
Two runs never overlap: the second says "Another run is still going; this one stops." A missed run catches up on the
next one. See [Schedule a page](../how-to/schedule-a-page.md).

chunks.heading: Features
chunks.text:
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `site:module:list <slug>` | Lists the website's optional features (modules): id, name and whether each one is on. |
| `site:module:enable <slug> <module>` | Turns a feature on, after updating the website's database for it. Refused while a feature it needs is off. |
| `site:module:disable <slug> <module> [--purge-data]` | Turns a feature off; its data is kept. Refused while a feature that is on needs it. `--purge-data` also deletes its data, for good. |

Features the installation set in `config/tenant.php` (`modules.locked`) can't be changed. See
[Turn features on or off](../how-to/turn-features-on-or-off.md).

chunks.heading: Roles
chunks.text:
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `site:role:list <slug>` | Lists the website's roles: name, label, how many people have each one and its permissions. |
| `site:role:create <slug> <name> [--label=] [--permissions=a,b]` | Creates a role. The name is lower-case letters, digits and `_`; the label defaults to the name. |
| `site:role:grant <slug> <role> <permission>` | Gives a role one more permission. |
| `site:role:revoke <slug> <role> <permission>` | Takes a permission away from a role. |
| `site:role:delete <slug> <role>` | Deletes a role nobody has. |

The rules of the **Roles** screen apply: Admin and Member can't be changed, the sign-up role only gets permissions
that are safe on sign-up, and only permissions of features that are on can be given. Changes are written to the
audit log. See [Create a custom role](../how-to/create-a-custom-role.md).

chunks.heading: Site search
chunks.text:
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `site:search:reindex <slug> [--locale=<locale>]` | Builds the website's search index again from its published pages, in every language or one. |
| `site:search:status <slug>` | How many pages the search index holds in each language, when it last changed, and whether it is waiting to be rebuilt. |
| `site:search <slug> <words> [--locale=<locale>] [--members]` | Searches the website the way a visitor would (`--members`: as someone signed in) and lists the first results. |

They refuse a website with search turned off. See [Search your website](../how-to/search-your-website.md).

chunks.heading: Analytics
chunks.text:
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `site:analytics:report <slug> [--from=YYYY-MM-DD] [--to=YYYY-MM-DD] [--report=<name>\|all] [--format=table\|csv\|json]` | Shows the website's analytics, the last 30 days by default. Reports: `summary`, `daily`, `pages`, `sources`, `languages`, `devices`, `searches`, `searches-without-results`, `not-found`, `bots`. Warns when the hourly roll-up hasn't run for two hours. |
| `site:analytics:purge <slug> [--before=YYYY-MM-DD]` | Deletes the figures from before a day; without `--before`, those older than the website keeps them. |

They refuse a website with analytics turned off. See [See who visits your website](../how-to/see-who-visits-your-website.md).

chunks.heading: AI assistant
chunks.text:
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `site:assistant:set <slug> --provider=<id> --model=<model> [--base-url=<address>] [--key-stdin]` | Chooses the AI service (`anthropic`, `openai`, `mistral` or `openai_compatible`) and model. With `--key-stdin` it reads the API key from standard input, so it never appears in the shell history: `printf %s "$KEY" \| bin/sightpress site:assistant:set …`. |
| `site:assistant:test <slug>` | Sends a tiny request and says whether the service answered. |
| `site:assistant:usage <slug> [--month=YYYY-MM]` | Shows the tokens used this month (or another), per task, and the budget. |
| `site:assistant:disable <slug> [--remove-key]` | Turns the assistant off for the website, and removes its key with `--remove-key`. |
| `assistant:ask <slug> "<question>"` | Asks the assistant a question from the console. |

They refuse a website with the assistant turned off; turn it on with `site:module:enable <slug> assistant`. See
[Use the AI assistant](../how-to/use-the-ai-assistant.md).

chunks.heading: Text messages
chunks.text:
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `site:sms:set <slug> --provider=<id> [--account=] [--sender=] [--region=] [--budget=] [--key-stdin]` | Sets up the website's text message provider (`twilio` or `vonage`, or a module's). With `--key-stdin` it reads the key from standard input: `printf %s "$KEY" \| bin/sightpress site:sms:set …`. `--budget` is message parts a month (0 = no limit). |
| `site:sms:remove <slug>` | Forgets the website's provider and key. |
| `site:sms:enable <slug>` | Turns text messages on. Refused until a provider is set up. |
| `site:sms:disable <slug>` | Turns text messages off. Numbers on accounts and the message log are kept. |
| `site:sms:test <slug> --to=<number>` | Sends a test message and says what happened. The number is only shown partly hidden. |

See [Set up text messages](../how-to/set-up-text-messages.md).

chunks.heading: Branding
chunks.text:
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `site:branding:set <slug> [--logo=] [--logo-alt=] [--icon=] [--share-image=] [--share-image-alt=]` | Uses picture files for the logo (SVG, PNG, JPEG or WebP, from 1:1 to 8:1 wide), the icon (a square PNG, JPEG or WebP of at least 512 × 512 pixels) or the share image (PNG, JPEG or WebP of 1200 × 630 pixels, or larger with the same proportions). The `-alt` options say what the picture shows, for screen readers; the default is the website's name. |
| `site:branding:reset <slug> [--logo] [--icon] [--share-image]` | Goes back to the generated logo, icon or share image; all three unless you name some. |

chunks.heading: Themes
chunks.text: See [Install and change a theme](../how-to/install-and-change-a-theme.md).

chunks.heading: theme:list
chunks.text:
```text
theme:list
```

Lists the installed themes: id, name, version, whether websites may use it (or why it can't be used), whether new
websites start with it, and the websites that use it. Websites whose theme isn't installed any more are listed as
errors; they are shown in the default theme.

chunks.heading: theme:validate
chunks.text:
```text
theme:validate [<theme>|<path>] [--axe]
```

Checks a theme the way it is checked before it is applied, and says what to fix:

- `theme.json` and the theme's manifest agree;
- the colour contrast passes in light and dark mode, with and without more contrast, chart colours included, against
  WCAG 2.2 AA, and the base font size is at least 16 px;
- the required templates are there, and the page shell includes SightPress's `<head>` partial;
- the theme ships no screenshot or preview output.

Give an installed theme's id or the folder of a theme. Without one, it checks every installed theme. `--axe` also
scans the theme's preview page with axe in light, dark and forced-colours mode; this needs Node.js and Playwright's
Chromium. It ends with an error when a check fails.

chunks.heading: theme:preview
chunks.text:
```text
theme:preview <theme|path> [--out=build/theme-preview/<id>] [--locale=en-GB] [--screenshot]
```

Writes the theme's preview page to a folder that opens in any browser without a server or an internet connection: a
top bar, a band with the theme's name and a Download button, one block of every kind, and the footer. `--screenshot`
also writes `screenshot.png`, `screenshot-dark.png` and `page.png` (needs Node.js and Playwright's Chromium). Theme
authors can run the same commands without a project with `vendor/bin/sightpress-theme`.

chunks.heading: site:theme:apply
chunks.text:
```text
site:theme:apply <site> <theme>
```

Applies an installed theme to a website. The theme must be allowed (`themes.allowed` in `config/tenant.php`) and pass
the checks of `theme:validate`. The website's activity log records the change.

chunks.heading: theme:publish-assets
chunks.text:
```text
theme:publish-assets [--no-screenshot]
```

Writes the preview page of every installed theme to `public/themes/<theme>/<version>/preview/`, with its screenshots
where Node.js and Chromium are installed, for the **Appearance** screen. The project runs it after `composer install`
and `composer update`.

chunks.heading: cache:clear
chunks.text:
```text
cache:clear
```

Empties the cache folder. Run it after installing or removing a theme or a module with Composer.

Everyone who signs in to a SightPress website has one **role**. A role is a set of **permissions**: each permission
lets a person do one thing, such as publish pages. Each website keeps its own people and roles, so someone can be an
editor on one website and a contributor on another.

chunks.heading: The four roles
chunks.text:
Every new website has these roles. The admin panel describes each one in the same words when you invite someone or
change their role.

| Role | What the admin panel says | In short |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Admin** | Can do everything, including inviting people, changing roles and site settings. | Runs the website. |
| **Editor** | Can write, review and publish any page, and invite contributors. | Looks after the content. |
| **Contributor** | Can write pages and send them for review, but not publish them. | Writes. |
| **Member** | Can sign in and read the site, but not use the admin panel. | Reads. |

The admin and member roles can't be renamed or deleted. The member role never has any permission. Every new website
has one admin: the person named when it was created (see [Create a website](../how-to/create-a-site.md)).

chunks.heading: Pages and roles
chunks.text:
Every page goes through the same steps before visitors can see it. Editors' own pages go through review too.

| Step | From | To | Who can take it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Submit for review** | Draft | Waiting for review | The person who wrote the page, or anyone who can edit any page |
| **Send back to draft** | Waiting for review | Draft | Editors and admins |
| **Approve** | Waiting for review | Approved | Editors and admins |
| **Publish** | Approved | Published | Editors and admins |
| **Unpublish** | Published | Draft | Editors and admins |

Only published pages are on the public website. When a page is submitted, every editor and admin (except the person
who submitted it) gets an e-mail about it. Contributors see their own pages and published pages in the admin panel,
and can't change a page while it waits for review.

chunks.heading: Who can invite whom
chunks.text:
- **Admins** can invite someone with any role.
- **Editors** can invite **contributors** only. Their form shows just that role.
- Contributors and members can't invite anyone.

The invited person gets an e-mail with a 6-digit code, never a link. See [Codes we send you](../how-to/codes-we-send-you.md).

chunks.heading: Change someone's role
chunks.text:
Admins do this in the admin panel:

1. Choose **People** in the admin menu. You should see a table of everyone with an account.
2. Choose the person's name.
3. Under **Change role**, choose the new role, then choose **Change role**. You should hear or see, for example,
   "Cleo’s role is now Editor." The new role applies from the person's next page.

On the same page, **Deactivate account** stops someone signing in straight away; their pages stay. **Reactivate**
lets them sign in again with their old password. Nobody can change their own role or deactivate themselves, so a
website always keeps someone who can manage people.

chunks.heading: Custom roles
chunks.text:
Admins (or anyone whose role may **Manage roles**) make their own roles on the **Roles** screen: a name, then the
permissions to tick, grouped by area, each with what it allows. Editor and Contributor can be changed too. Admin
always has every permission and Member never has one, so those two can't be changed. Permissions of features that
are off aren't listed, and roles keep them. Nobody can take **Manage roles** away from their own role, and a role
that someone has can't be deleted. Step by step: [Create a custom role](../how-to/create-a-custom-role.md).

chunks.heading: For developers
chunks.text:
Permission names, for modules and the command line: `admin.access`, `page.create`, `page.edit.own`, `page.edit.any`,
`page.submit`, `page.publish`, `page.archive`, `page.delete`, `media.upload`, `media.publish`, `menu.manage`,
`user.invite`, `user.manage`, `role.manage`, `settings.manage`, `module.manage`, `theme.apply` and `audit.view`.

- A role that has any permission also has `admin.access`.
- A module adds permissions with `$registrar->permissions()->add(...)`. They are copied into every website and given
  to their default roles, and always to the admin role.
- The role people get when they register themselves (site setting `registration_role`, default `member`) may only
  hold permissions that are safe for strangers: `admin.access`, `page.create`, `page.edit.own`, `page.submit` and
  `media.upload`. Self-registration arrives in a later version.

Every public page of a SightPress website is ready for search engines and for AI search engines and assistants, with
nothing to set up. This page explains what SightPress does for each page, and the settings that change it.

chunks.heading: Which pages are shown
What every page has
chunks.text:
- **A title**: the page's "Title in search results" if it has one, otherwise its title followed by the website's
  name, such as "About us - Riverside Library".
- **A description**: the page's "Description for search engines", otherwise its summary, otherwise its first words.
  Longer text is cut at a whole word, at 160 characters. Social networks get the same description.
- **One address** (the canonical address). An address ending in `/` moves permanently to the one without it, and the
  website's other domains move permanently to its first domain.
- **Structured data** that search engines read: the page, where it sits in the website, who runs the website (from
  the site settings) and the pictures, videos and recordings on it.
- **"Last updated"** under the content, in the reader's time zone.
- **A Markdown version** for AI readers: add `.md` to the page's address, such as `/about.md`, or `/index.md` for the
  home page. It has the title, the summary, every block as plain text (pictures with their alternative text, videos
  and recordings with their transcripts, files with their type and size) and the page's address and date. Contact
  forms are left out.

chunks.heading: Files for search engines and AI readers
chunks.text:
| Address | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `/sitemap.xml` | Every page search engines may list, in every language, with the date it last changed. |
| `/robots.txt` | Keeps crawlers out of the admin panel, accounts and sign-in pages, points them to the sitemap, and names the AI crawlers the website keeps out. |
| `/llms.txt` | The website's name and summary, then a link to the Markdown version of every page that may be listed, with its description. |
| `/llms-full.txt` | The same pages in full, as Markdown, up to 500 KB. If it stops early, it says how many pages were left out. |

The files are made again each time a page is created, saved, moved, published or unpublished.

chunks.heading: Settings
chunks.text: Admins change these under **Site settings**, in the **Search & AI** section.

chunks.heading: AI crawlers
chunks.text:
Whether AI services may read the public pages, to answer people's questions with a link back (AI search and
assistants) and to train their models.

| Choice | What `robots.txt` asks |
| --- | --- |
| **Allow all** (the default) | Nothing extra: every crawler may read the public pages. |
| **AI search only** | Crawlers that train AI models, such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended and CCBot, stay out. AI search and assistants may read the pages and link to them. |
| **Block all** | Every AI crawler stays out: those that train models, and AI search and assistant crawlers such as OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot. |

Search engines are never affected. `robots.txt` is a request that well-behaved crawlers follow, not a lock.

chunks.heading: Search console codes
chunks.text:
To prove to a search engine that the website is yours, it gives you a code. Paste only the code (the part in
`content="…"`) into **Google Search Console verification code**, **Bing Webmaster Tools verification code** or
**Yandex Webmaster verification code**. SightPress adds it to the home page.

chunks.heading: IndexNow
chunks.text:
**Tell search engines at once when a page is published or unpublished (IndexNow)** is off by default. When it is on,
the website tells the search engines that use IndexNow, such as Bing and Yandex, each time a page is published or
unpublished.

chunks.heading: Who runs the site
chunks.text:
The **Who runs the site** section (a description, full name, contact details and profiles on other websites) goes
into the structured data, and the description also goes at the top of `llms.txt`. Leave a field empty to keep it
private.

chunks.heading: Settings on each page
chunks.text:
In the page editor's **Search & AI** section:

| Field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Summary** | One or two sentences, shown in lists of pages, used as the description when there is none, and read by AI search engines. |
| **Title in search results** | Replaces the title in search results only. |
| **Description for search engines** | Shown under the title in search results. About 160 characters are shown. |
| **Picture shown when the page is shared** | A picture from the media library. Leave it empty to use the website's share image. Shown only when the media library has pictures. |
| **Ask search engines and AI search engines not to list this page** | Keeps the page out of search results, the sitemap, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`. |
| **Address of the original** | Only for a copy of a page on another website: its full address. The copy then points search engines to the original, and is left out of the sitemap. |

Before publishing, the page's checks suggest a description and a summary when they are missing, and warn about a
description longer than 160 characters or a title another page already has.

chunks.heading: Check a website from the command line
chunks.text:
```sh
docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:seo:check demo
```

It lists titles longer than 60 characters, missing or too long descriptions, pages left out of search and why, and
whether SightPress runs in production. Two pages with the same title count as a problem, and the command ends with an
error.

`config/tenant.php` holds the settings for **every website** of a SightPress installation. It returns a PHP array.
Every key is optional: a missing key gets the default shown here. SightPress checks the file each time it starts, and
a value it can't use stops it with a message that names the key and says what it should be.

Keys and passwords never go in this file. They come from environment variables (in the `skeleton` folder, from
`.env`), which are listed at the end.

chunks.text:

| --- | --- | --- |
| `registry.path` | `config/sites.php` | The site registry: every website, its domains and its database. Only `bin/sightpress site:*` commands write it. |
| `sites_dir` | `sites` | Where websites keep their files, when they are stored locally. |
| `cache_dir` | `var/cache/<APP_ENV>` | The cache. `bin/sightpress cache:clear` empties it. |

| `log.level` | `notice` | The least important messages that are written: `debug`, `info`, `notice`, `warning`, `error` … |
| `session.path` | `var/sessions` | Where sign-in sessions are kept. |
| `session.idle_timeout` | `7200` | Seconds without a request after which someone is signed out (at least 60). |

chunks.text:

| --- | --- | --- |

| `timezone` | `UTC` | The time zone of new websites, as a name such as `Europe/London`. |

chunks.text:

See [Turn features on or off](../how-to/turn-features-on-or-off.md), [Add a module](../how-to/add-a-module.md) and

In this tutorial you make a SightPress module of your own: **Events**. Each event gets a page on the website, with
structured data search engines understand and a Markdown version for AI readers. Admins add events on an Events
screen, editors can put an event card on any page, and events appear in the sitemap, in `llms.txt` and in site search.
You start from the module template, write the module, test it, install it on a website and publish it.

You need some experience with PHP and the command line, and:

- PHP 8.5 and Composer 2;
- a SightPress project to try the module in (see [Getting started](../getting-started.md)).

A module only uses `sightpress/module-interface`, the contract between SightPress and its modules. It never depends
on SightPress itself, so it keeps working when SightPress changes inside.

chunks.heading: 1. Create your module from the template
chunks.text:
```sh
composer create-project sightpress/module-template events
cd events
composer check
```

`composer check` runs the code style, static analysis, the unit tests (every line of `src/` must be tested) and an
integration test that installs the module in SightPress and turns it off and on. Each check should pass.

On GitHub, you can instead open the [module template](https://github.com/sightpress/module-template) and choose
**Use this template**, then clone your new repository and run `composer install`.

chunks.heading: 10. Test it
11. Install it on a website
chunks.text:
In your SightPress project, add the module as a Composer path repository while you work on it:

```sh
composer config repositories.events '{"type": "path", "url": "../events", "options": {"symlink": true}}'
composer require acme/events:@dev
bin/sightpress cache:clear
bin/sightpress site:module:list <site>
```

`site:module:list` shows `acme.events (Events): on` for new websites. On an existing website, turn it on with

```sh
bin/sightpress site:module:enable <site> acme.events
```

or, as an admin, on the **Features** screen (**Turn on Events**). Turning it on runs its migration. Then open
**Events** in the admin panel and add the first event.

If something is wrong with the module (a typo in `composer.json`, a class that doesn't load), SightPress keeps
running: the Features screen, `site:module:list` and `system:check` list it as unavailable, with the reason.

chunks.heading: 12. Publish it
chunks.text:
1. Put the module in its own Git repository and push it to GitHub (or any Git host).
2. Tag a version, for example `0.1.0`. With the template's release workflow, merging the release pull request does it.
3. Sign in to [Packagist](https://packagist.org/), choose **Submit** and give your repository's address. Keep the
   `sightpress-module` keyword, so people can find it.

Anyone can then install it with `composer require acme/events`.

chunks.heading: Next steps
chunks.text:
- Add a setting with `$registrar->settings()`, a scheduled job with `$registrar->schedule()`, or listen to SightPress
  events (a page was published, a module was turned on) with `$registrar->subscribers()`.
- Translate the texts: copy `acme_events.en-GB.xlf` to another language and change each `target`.
- Read the README of the module template for the rules every module follows: accessible screens, plain words,
  portable migrations and as little personal data as possible.

In this tutorial you make a SightPress theme of your own, "Harbour". You start from the theme template, change its
colours, override a template, add a layout, check and preview it, install it on a website, and publish it. You need
some experience with the command line, PHP and CSS. The template already has everything a theme needs, and the checks
tell you in words when something isn't right.

You need:

- PHP 8.5 and Composer 2;
- a SightPress project to try the theme in (see [Getting started](../getting-started.md));
- for screenshots only: Node.js and Playwright's Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium`).

chunks.heading: 1. Create your theme from the template
chunks.text:
```sh
composer create-project sightpress/theme-template harbour
cd harbour
composer check
```

You should see each check pass, ending with:

```text
The theme "My theme" passes: 172 colour pairs checked in light and dark mode, with and without more contrast; the base font size is at least 16 px; the required templates are there; it ships no screenshot.
```

On GitHub, you can instead open the [theme template](https://github.com/sightpress/theme-template) and choose
**Use this template**, then clone your new repository and run `composer install`.

chunks.heading: 2. Make it yours
chunks.text:
A theme has an id: lower-case words joined by hyphens, starting with your vendor name. Ours is `acme-harbour`.

1. In `composer.json`, change `name` to `acme/theme-harbour`, and write your own `description` and `homepage`.
2. In `src/MyTheme.php`, change `ID` to `acme-harbour`. Change the name to `Harbour` and write a description of one
   or two sentences. Fill in `author`.
3. In `theme.json`, change `name` to `acme-harbour` and `label` to `Harbour`.
4. Write `previewDescription`: what the top of your theme's preview page looks like, for people who can't see its
   screenshot. Describe the look, not the file. For example: "A dark blue top bar with the site name in white, a pale
   blue band with a large heading and a yellow Download button."

The template's README lists the rest: renaming the class and its namespace when you want to.

chunks.heading: 3. Change the colours
chunks.text:
Colours are design tokens in `theme.json`, one set for light mode and one for dark mode. Try a light blue for buttons
and highlights in light mode:

```json
"primary": "#7fb3ff",
```

Run the checks:

```sh
composer check
```

They fail, and say why:

```text
The theme "Harbour" fails with 3 problems:
1. In light mode, text "on-primary" (#ffffff) on "primary" (#7fb3ff) has a contrast of 2.14:1; it needs at least 4.50:1.
2. In light mode, interface colour "primary" (#7fb3ff) on "background" (#ffffff) has a contrast of 2.14:1; it needs at least 3.00:1.
3. In light mode, interface colour "primary" (#7fb3ff) on "surface" (#f3f4f6) has a contrast of 1.94:1; it needs at least 3.00:1.
```

White text on a light blue is too hard to read, and the light blue itself is hard to see on the white page. Use a darker blue, and run the checks again:

```json
"primary": "#0b4f8a",
```

Every colour pair in the `contrast` section of `theme.json` is checked in light and dark mode, with and without "more
contrast": text needs 4.5:1, borders and other interface colours 3:1. Chart colours are always checked.

chunks.heading: 4. Override a template
chunks.text:
A theme's templates are in `templates/`. Change the footer of every page: in `templates/master.html.twig`, replace the `footer` block with: ```twig {% block footer %}

{{ site_name }}, made with the Harbour theme.

{% endblock %} ``` A template you don't have comes from the default theme, so you only keep the ones you change. Keep the shell's skip link, its landmarks and `{% include '@seo/head.html.twig' %}`: the checks refuse a shell without that line, because it holds every page's description, canonical address and structured data.

chunks.heading: 5. Add a layout
6. Check it
chunks.text:
```sh
composer check
```

Besides the code style, static analysis and tests, this runs `theme:validate`, the checks SightPress runs before it
applies a theme. It also refuses a screenshot or a `build/` folder that would end up in your package.

chunks.heading: 7. Preview it
chunks.text:
```sh
composer preview
```

Open `build/theme-preview/acme-harbour/index.html` in any browser. It works offline and needs no PHP. It is the same
page for every theme, so you can compare them:

- a top bar with links to each part of the page;
- a band with your theme's name, description and a **Download** button;
- one block of every kind;
- the footer.

Go through it with the keyboard alone, at 200% and 400% zoom, in dark mode and with a contrast theme.

With Node.js and Chromium installed, `composer preview -- --screenshot` also writes `screenshot.png`,
`screenshot-dark.png` and `page.png` in the same folder. Use them for your README. Never commit them: your theme's
releases get them attached automatically.

chunks.heading: 8. Try it on a website
chunks.text:
In your SightPress project, add the theme as a path repository, so changes show up as you make them:

```sh
composer config repositories.harbour '{"type": "path", "url": "../harbour", "options": {"symlink": true}}'
composer require acme/theme-harbour:@dev
bin/sightpress cache:clear
bin/sightpress theme:validate acme-harbour
```

Then apply it, from the command line:

```sh
bin/sightpress site:theme:apply demo acme-harbour
```

or in the admin panel, under **Appearance**: choose **Use Harbour**. If pages use a layout your theme doesn't have,
SightPress lists them first. To see the screenshot in the theme picker, run `bin/sightpress theme:publish-assets`.

chunks.heading: 9. Open a pull request
chunks.text:
Push your theme to GitHub and open a pull request with a change. The template's workflows add two things:

- **a download**: the preview page, its screenshots and an accessibility report, in one zip;
- **a comment** on the pull request with the download link, your `previewDescription` and the accessibility result in
  light mode, dark mode and forced colours.

A reviewer can judge the change without installing anything (see [Review a theme change](../how-to/review-a-theme-change.md)).

chunks.heading: 10. Publish it
chunks.text:
1. Merge your pull requests. Release Please keeps a release pull request open; merging it tags the release and
   attaches the preview and the screenshots to it.
2. Submit your repository on [packagist.org](https://packagist.org/packages/submit) and turn on its GitHub hook (or
   add the `PACKAGIST_USERNAME` and `PACKAGIST_API_TOKEN` secrets the release workflow uses).
3. Anyone running SightPress can now install your theme with `composer require acme/theme-harbour`.

That's it: you have made, checked, previewed, applied and published a theme.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.text:
SightPress is a content management system (CMS): a program that lets you build and run websites without writing code.
You write pages in an admin panel, and SightPress turns them into a website that everyone can use, including people
who use a screen reader, a keyboard alone or screen magnification.

This page explains what SightPress can do today, then gives you ideas for websites you could build with it.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: What you can do today
chunks.text:
SightPress is still at an early stage, and this page follows the newest documentation. It describes version 0.5.
SightPress already gives you the following.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: Run many websites from one installation
chunks.text:
One installation of SightPress can run as many websites as you need. Each website has its own pages, people, files,
menus and settings, and its own main language. A person can be an editor on one website and a contributor on another.
See [Create a website](how-to/create-a-site.md).

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: Write pages with blocks
chunks.text:
A page is a list of **blocks**, such as a heading, some text or a picture. There are thirteen kinds:

| Block | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| Heading | Starting a part of the page. |
| Text | Paragraphs, lists, links, quotes and more. |
| Image | One picture, with its alternative text and a caption. |
| Gallery | A set of up to 50 pictures. |
| Video | A video with captions and a transcript. It never starts by itself. |
| Audio | A sound recording, such as a podcast episode, with a transcript. |
| File download | A file such as a PDF, with its type and size shown in the link. |
| Call to action | A button that leads somewhere, such as "Book a visit". |
| Columns | Two to four columns side by side on wide screens. |
| Contact form | A form visitors use to send you a message, without a puzzle to solve. |
| Video or map from another site | A YouTube or Vimeo video, or an OpenStreetMap map. Nothing loads from the other site until the reader asks. |
| List of pages | The pages under a page, or the latest changed pages, as a list or as cards. It keeps itself up to date. |
| Sign language video | A video in a sign language, such as British Sign Language, with captions. |

Each block can also have its own look, such as a background, a width or the space around it. SightPress makes sure
text stays readable on every background.

Every block is described in [Blocks](reference/blocks.md).

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: Publish with confidence
chunks.text:
- **Accessibility checks.** Before a page is published, SightPress checks it. A picture with no alternative text, a
  video with speech but no captions or text that is too faint to read stops the page from being published until it
  is fixed. Smaller problems, such as a link that says "click here", come up as suggestions.
- **Review before publishing.** Contributors write pages and send them for review. Editors and admins approve and
  publish them. See [Write and publish a page](how-to/write-and-publish-a-page.md).
- **Roles for your team.** Admins, editors, contributors and members each see and do only what they need. See
  [Roles and permissions](reference/roles-and-permissions.md).
- **Your own roles.** Make a role with exactly the permissions someone needs, such as "Events editor". See
  [Create a custom role](how-to/create-a-custom-role.md).
- **Confirm important changes.** A website can ask for a code sent by text before changes such as changing someone's
  role or deleting data. See [Confirm important changes](how-to/confirm-important-changes.md).
- **An audit log.** Admins can see who changed what, and when.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: Look after your files and people
chunks.text:
- **A media library** for pictures, videos, sound recordings, captions files and documents. Visitors only see the
  files you publish.
- **Invitations.** Invite people by e-mail. They get a 6-digit code, never a link. See
  [Codes we send you](how-to/codes-we-send-you.md).
- **Menus.** A main menu and a footer menu, which you change in the admin panel.
- **Site settings.** The website's name, profile, logo and other details.
- **Keep websites to your organisation.** Allow only your organisation's email addresses, and let colleagues register
  on members-only websites with their work email. See
  [Keep websites to your organisation](how-to/keep-websites-to-your-organisation.md).
- **Text messages.** Once whoever runs SightPress sets up a text message provider, people can get notifications by
  text and [sign in with their phone](how-to/sign-in-with-your-phone.md). See
  [Set up text messages](how-to/set-up-text-messages.md).

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: Be found in search engines and AI search
chunks.text:
Every public page is ready for search engines and for AI search engines and assistants, with nothing to set up: a
title and description, a sitemap, structured data and a plain-text version of each page. You choose whether AI
services may read your pages. See [Search and AI visibility](reference/search-and-ai.md).

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: Do every task with a keyboard and a screen reader
chunks.text:
The admin panel, the default theme and every built-in feature aim to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines
(WCAG) 2.2 at level AA. Nothing depends on dragging, on colour alone or on a puzzle to prove you are human. Admins can
also do many tasks with the [command line tool](reference/command-line.md).

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: Reach more people and understand your visitors
chunks.text:
- **Several languages.** Publish a website in more than one language. See
  [Add a language and translate a page](how-to/add-a-language.md).
- **Site search.** Visitors can search your pages. See [Search your website](how-to/search-your-website.md).
- **Analytics.** See how many people visit and what they read. See
  [See who visits your website](how-to/see-who-visits-your-website.md).
- **An AI assistant.** Turn it on if you want help drafting, with your own API key. A person checks every suggestion.
  See [Use the AI assistant](how-to/use-the-ai-assistant.md).

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: Choose how your website looks and where its files live
chunks.text:
- **Themes and colours.** Install other themes, and change the colours on the **Appearance** screen.
  See [Install and change a theme](how-to/install-and-change-a-theme.md).
- **Large files.** Send big files in parts, and pause or resume them. See
  [Upload large files](how-to/upload-large-files.md).
- **Cloud storage and a CDN.** Keep a website's files with an S3-compatible service, and deliver public
  files from near each visitor.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: Add features with modules
chunks.text:
Install add-on **modules** made by others, and turn each one on only for the websites that need it. A module that
is broken or missing never stops your websites. See [Add a module](how-to/add-a-module.md). Developers can build their
own: see [Create a module](tutorials/create-a-module.md).

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: Ideas for websites
chunks.text: These ideas use only what SightPress can do today. Each one lists the blocks and features that help most.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: A website for a small business
chunks.text:
A café, a hairdresser, a plumber or a shop that wants people to find it and get in touch.

- Pages: Home, What we offer, Prices, About us, Contact.
- A **Gallery** of your work or your premises, and a **Call to action** such as "Book an appointment" that opens a
  phone number or an e-mail address.
- A **Contact form**, so that customers can write to you without seeing your e-mail address.
- **Search and AI visibility**, so that people asking a search engine or an AI assistant can find you.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: A charity or community group
chunks.text:
A charity, a residents' association, a sports club or a support group.

- Pages: Who we are, What we do, Get involved, Annual reports, Contact.
- **File download** blocks for annual reports, minutes and leaflets, with their type and size shown.
- A **Video** about your work, with captions and a transcript, so that everyone can follow it.
- A **List of pages** on the home page that shows your latest news by itself.
- **Roles**, so that volunteers write pages as contributors and a trustee publishes them as an editor.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: A podcast or audio project
chunks.text:
A podcast, an audio drama, a radio show or a collection of oral history recordings.

- One page per episode, with an **Audio** block and its transcript. The transcript makes every episode readable and
  searchable.
- A **File download** for show notes or extra material.
- A page for each guest or contributor, with an **Image** and a short biography.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: A portfolio
chunks.text:
An artist, photographer, writer, musician or designer who wants to show their work.

- A **Gallery** for each project, with alternative text that describes every picture. Writing good alternative text
  helps blind and low-vision visitors enjoy your work, and helps search engines understand it.
- **Columns** to put a picture next to its description on wide screens.
- **Audio** or **Video** blocks for performances and recordings.
- A **Contact form** for commissions and bookings.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: A school, library or museum
chunks.text:
A school, a public library, a museum or a gallery that must be accessible to everyone.

- Pages: Visit us, Opening hours, What's on, Accessibility, Contact.
- **Video** tours with captions, and **Audio** guides with transcripts.
- **File download** blocks for policies, timetables and forms.
- **Roles**, so that staff in different departments write their own pages, and a web editor approves them.
- One installation with a separate **website** for each school, branch or venue.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: An accessibility-first information website
chunks.text:
A council service, a health clinic, a disability organisation or a guide to a local service, where clear,
accessible information matters most.

- Short pages with clear **Headings**, so that screen reader users can jump from part to part.
- **File download** blocks for forms and leaflets, plus the same information as a page, so that nobody has to open a
  PDF.
- A **Sign language video** of the most important pages, with captions.
- The **accessibility checks** stop common mistakes, such as a missing caption, before they reach the public.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: A personal website or blog-style journal
chunks.text:
A personal homepage, a CV or a journal of your projects, travels or hobbies.

- Pages: About me, Projects, CV, Contact.
- A **File download** for your CV as a PDF.
- One page per project or trip, with **Images**, a **Gallery** and **Text**.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: Several websites for an agency or organisation
chunks.text:
A web agency, a federation of clubs or an organisation with several brands.

- One installation of SightPress with a **website** for each client, club or brand, each with its own domain,
  language, people and settings.
- Each website keeps its own **roles**, so that each client or club looks after its own content.
- The **command line tool** to create and list websites quickly.
- **Domain and email policies**, so that every website and every account stays within your organisation.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: Coming later
chunks.text:
Later versions of SightPress add more, such as tools to download or delete someone's personal data and a guide to
putting SightPress on a public server.
The [Getting started](getting-started.md) guide and the [how-to guides](how-to/index.md) are updated as each feature
arrives.

chunks.page: What you can build with SightPress
chunks.heading: Where to go next
chunks.text:
- To decide which options and content suit your website, read [Plan your website](how-to/plan-a-site.md).
- To try SightPress on your own computer, follow [Getting started](getting-started.md).
- To build your first website, follow [Create a website](how-to/create-a-site.md), then
  [Write and publish a page](how-to/write-and-publish-a-page.md).
